**Feasibility:**
- Perf risk: medium
- iOS risk: medium
- Blender MCP can produce: yes
- Blocker: INTEGRATION SNIPPET IS BROKEN — WRONG mkPhys SIGNATURE. The plan's code does `group.traverse(c => { mkPhys(THREE, c.material); ... })`. Verified in src/lib/3d/mobilePerf.ts:339 the real signature is `mkPhys(three, props)` — it CONSTRUCTS a new material from a plain-props object and RETURNS it; it does NOT mutate an existing material in place. Passing a live THREE.Material instance as `props` and discarding the return value is a no-op on desktop and on mobile builds a MeshStandardMaterial from a Material-as-dict (maps/uniforms mostly lost). The GLB materials would therefore NEVER be mobile-stripped, and the returned material is thrown away. This is a hard functional bug that must be rewritten before any build.
- Blocker: loadModel() DOES NOT re-apply mkPhys, DOES NOT set aoMap.channel, DOES NOT dedupe materials. Verified src/lib/3d/modelLoader.ts:17-45 only sets castShadow/receiveShadow. The plan asserts 'zero changes to modelLoader.ts' AND relies on post-load traversal to fix materials/AO — but the traversal code is the broken snippet above. Net: without a corrected post-load pass, GLB materials render as raw MeshStandardMaterial from GLTFLoader with aoMap on the default UV1 channel (assetLoader hardcodes channel 0 at line 554 for procedural sets, but GLTFLoader-loaded textures keep glTF's own channel mapping) → AO may sample wrong/absent UV, breaking mobile/potato shading which depends on baked AO.
- Blocker: GLTFLoader `.clone()` SHARES materials & geometry (Three.js clone is shallow for materials). Verified modelLoader returns `model.clone()`. For a singleton dome this is benign, but the plan's traverse mutates `c.material.aoMap.channel` on the SHARED cached material — if the dome GLB is ever loaded a 2nd time (SPA re-mount before clearModelCache) the mutation double-applies / races. Must guard mutation to run once, or clone materials.
- Blocker: GOVERNOR WARMUP MATH IS WRONG. Plan claims 'defer materialisation one rAF past the 2.5s warmup dead-zone.' Verified GOV_WARMUP_MS=2500 in mobilePerf.ts:240 — ONE requestAnimationFrame is ~16ms, nowhere near 2500ms. The DRACO decode + GPU upload will almost certainly land INSIDE warmup regardless (good for hiding the upload stall) but the STEADY-STATE cost of ~34k-tri desktop / ~4.8k mobile dome is measured across the full GOV_SAMPLE_MS=15000 window; the mitigation as written buys nothing and misstates the mechanism.
- Blocker: MOBILE TIER, NOT 'iOS-collapses-to-mobile', IS THE BINDING GATE — AND THE DOME'S ~4.8k MOBILE LOD IS FINE, BUT THE DRAW-CALL CLAIM IS UNVERIFIED. perfAssert.ts:21 hardcodes MOBILE_DRAW_CALL_BUDGET=150 total/frame (not the plan's 80). The plan claims '−16 draw calls mobile' by replacing ~30 procedural primitives. But the procedural dome primitives are added to centralGroup and may be swept up by an existing mergeGeometries pass — if they are ALREADY merged into a shared draw call, hiding them via visible=false does NOT free draw calls, and ADDING 2 GLB meshes is net +2 calls, not −16. The 'net negative draw calls' claim needs verification against the actual merge pass before it can be trusted.
- Fix: Rewrite the post-load material pass with the CORRECT mkPhys contract. mkPhys(three,props) returns a NEW material — it cannot fix a GLTF material in place. Either (a) do NOT call mkPhys at all and instead manually strip Physical-only props / ensure the GLB ships MeshStandard (author standard PBR only, which the plan already mandates, so mkPhys is unnecessary for GLB), OR (b) rebuild each material via `c.material = mkPhys(THREE, {color, map, normalMap, roughnessMap, aoMap, roughness, metalness, ...})` reading fields off the loaded material. Given the plan already authors standard PBR (no clearcoat/transmission), the simplest correct fix is: DROP the mkPhys call entirely and just set `c.material.aoMap && (c.material.aoMap.channel = 0)`, `envMapIntensity`, and force MeshStandardMaterial at export. Ship glass as MeshStandardMaterial(transparent,opacity 0.7) in Blender — never KHR_materials_transmission.
- Fix: Set aoMap.channel=0 correctly and confirm the GLB exports a SINGLE TEXCOORD_0. Bake AO to UV0 only; assert at export that there is exactly one UV set. Verify at runtime that GLTFLoader-loaded aoMap.channel is forced to 0 (it defaults to the glTF-declared TEXCOORD index).
- Fix: Correct the palette targets to CANON. canon.ts confirms GOLD='#D4AF37' (plan correct; brief's #B8973A is stale). But the EXISTING W2 shell is ochre '#A5674E' roughness 0.82 (ExteriorScene.tsx:1798-1799), NOT '#B0725A' matte. Decide deliberately: either match the shipped W2 ochre so the GLB does not clash with adjacent procedural roofs, or intentionally re-grade ALL terracotta scene-wide. Bake at exposure 1.0 (EXPOSURE=1.15 confirmed applied once in postprocessing.ts:108).
- Fix: Fix the line-reference drift in the plan before authoring. The plan cites the W2 dome at lines 1747-1903 with vars rDomeR/rDrumR/rDrumH/drumBaseY — VERIFIED correct (1747-1823). But it ALSO references a 'smooth SphereGeometry + Box rib + primitive cone' variant that matches the DIFFERENT block at lines 785-831 (bDrumR/bDomeR — likely the W1/non-W2 path). The tagging pass (userData.w2DomePart=true) must target the ACTUAL W2 meshes (rDome at 1807, drum at 1770, pilasters 1778, drum windows 1787, lantern 1815+), not the W1 block, or the procedural crown will not hide under W3.
- Fix: Verify the draw-call baseline empirically before claiming 'net negative'. Add the dev overlay (renderer.info.render.calls/triangles) FIRST, capture the W2 baseline at WP3, then confirm whether procedural dome primitives are pre-merged. If they are merged, budget the 2-4 GLB meshes as ADDITIVE (+2-4 calls) and confirm total stays <150 mobile. If not, confirm the visible=false sweep actually drops calls.
- Fix: Fix the warmup-jank mitigation: to move the GPU upload OUT of the measured steady-state, materialise BEFORE GOV_WARMUP_MS=2500 (i.e. upload during warmup so the stall is ignored) — the opposite of the plan's wording. Kick the fetch synchronously at mount so DRACO decode (~40ms) completes and the add(group) happens well before 2500ms. Confirm the reduced-motion stills at WP1/WP3/WP5 have the GLB resolved (fetch<300ms is optimistic on cold cache/3G — add a still-recompose-on-load hook or the stills bake the procedural dome).
- Fix: POTATO GUARD: getQuality()/governor can demote desktop→mobile→potato mid-session (mobilePerf.ts:283). Read the EFFECTIVE tier (getQuality-derived), not native getGPUTier(), before choosing LOD; and early-return the GLB load entirely when effective tier is potato (plan says this — keep it). Confirm POTATO_QUALITY.shadowsEnabled=false (verified line 183) so DomePotato must read with baked AO and no shadow/env reliance.
- Fix: Confirm Hunyuan3D/Rodin N-panel generators are enabled + commercial license, OR commit up-front to the scripted SCREW-modifier acanthus fallback. Both generators are currently DISABLED per the routing doctrine; the dome itself is 100% scripted bpy (safe), so gate the ONLY generative touch (capital acanthus) behind an explicit owner enablement or ship the parametric fallback. This does not block the dome shell/drum/lantern, which are fully producible via execute_blender_code today.

**Acceptance criteria:**
- [ ] GLB loads via existing loadModel() with NO changes to modelLoader.ts; header asserts pass (magic/v2/KHR_draco); two bust GLBs still load (decoder canary intact).
- [ ] Dev overlay confirms renderer.info.render.triangles < 750k AND renderer.info.render.calls < 150 on mobile at WP3 AFTER integration (measured, not assumed). If the procedural dome primitives were pre-merged, the 2-4 GLB meshes are budgeted as additive and total still < 150.

- [ ] DomePotato path: when getQuality() reports potato (shadowsEnabled=false, vegetationDensity=0), the GLB load is skipped entirely and the procedural dome is used; no GLB GPU cost on potato.

### WS03 — Casa-torri (7) + 2 gate towers

*Hill-town tower cluster: varied heights, string courses, machicolations, belvedere tops, gate-tower flanking the entrance.*

**Summary:** WS03 casa-torri kit = 3 scripted-BPY DRACO GLBs (tower_cap, campanile_cap, bifora_window) replacing only the cheapest-reading tower crowns/belfry/bifora on DESKTOP, gated by flag3d('w3_exterior') AND not-isMobileGPU; mobile/potato stay byte-identical procedural; materials re-pointed by NAME to already-warm stoneTex/roofTileTex plus one baked 512px AO on UV0; campanile apex authored to the VERIFIED shipped 29.7 local (NOT the wrong sub-27), safely under the 31.7 dome apex.</oneLineSummary>
<parameter name="targetPath">public/models/exterior/tower_cap.glb, campanile_cap.glb, bifora_window.glb
**Priority `P2` · ~4.5d · Feasible: yes · Confidence 0.72**

**Vision.** Lift the 6 procedural casa-torri (5 plain towers + 1 west clock campanile) from box-stacked BufferGeometry to a tight 3-GLB Blender kit that reads as hand-cut Tuscan masonry at the tympanum name-beat (WP3, d=118), while staying draw-call-flat on mobile and byte-identical on potato. Strategy = HYBRID surgical replacement (brief 3) as the spine, executed with PHOTOREAL-MAX baked-normal fidelity (brief 1) on desktop, under PERF-FIRST governor discipline (brief 2). Keep the strongest procedural systems (BoxGeometry shafts merged into gWall, quoin chains into gTrimM, plinths, ivy/stain/moss overlays, anchors) and replace ONLY the parts that read cheapest at the camera angles that matter: the flat coppo hip-roof caps, the boxes-in-a-box campanile belfry/cupola/lantern crown, and the flat-slot bifora windows. Minimum intervention, ~10x perceived-fidelity lift, byte-identical procedural fallback on any reject.

**Design decisions:**
- SCOPE = 6 TOWERS, NOT 9. VERIFIED: TOWERS[] in ExteriorScene.tsx (line 2931) is exactly 6 entries: [-38,-24 campanile], [34,-24], [-50,16], [46,16], [-26,37], [22,37]. The masterplan aspirationally cites 7 casa-torri + 2 gate towers, but the shipped W2 geometry has 6. Author for the 6 that exist: 1 campanile instance + 5 plain-tower cap instances. Do not model to the aspirational count.
- HYBRID CAP-ONLY SPLIT beats full-shaft replacement (rejects the shaft GLBs in briefs 1 and 2). VERIFIED at lines 2939-2958: tower shaft (gWall), quoin chains + crown (gTrimM), serena bands (gSerenaM) and plinths (gPlinthM) are pushed into shared buckets that ALSO carry the corps, wings and balustrades. You cannot surgically remove tower-shaft tris from a post-merge BufferGeometry, so a full-shaft GLB forces either z-fight overlay or a fragile skip-flag threaded through every push. The caps/belfry/bifora are cleanly separable. Replace those three; keep the shafts procedural.
- TRACK CAP GEOMETRY IN A SEPARATE ARRAY TO AVOID DOUBLE-RENDER. Before the TOWERS.forEach loop, introduce a gCapProcedural[] collector; route the per-tower crown-cornice, campanile belfry/cupola/lantern, and bifora sub-geometries into it instead of directly into gTrimM/gSerenaM/gRoofDS/gWallD. If W3 resolves, those arrays are simply never merged; if W3 is OFF or the GLB rejects, they merge exactly as today. This is cleaner than post-merge splicing (brief 1) and needs no skip-return threaded through shaft pushes (brief 2).
- GLBs EMBED NO TEXTURES; RE-POINT MATERIALS TO ALREADY-WARM PBR SETS (adopt brief 3's zero-fetch contract). VERIFIED at lines 278-281: roofTileTex=loadTerracottaTileTextures([3,3]) and stoneTex=loadPlasterWallTextures([4,4]) are already loaded synchronously. After loadModel, traverse and assign map/normalMap/roughnessMap/aoMap by explicit slot index from those cached sets. Net new over-the-wire = 3 tiny DRACO GLBs (<60KB total), zero new HTTP texture requests, zero new mobile eager texture slots. This resolves the brief-1 texture-budget-collision risk outright: no stone_masonry/terracotta_roof PBR set is shipped.
- DESKTOP-ONLY GLB PATH; MOBILE + POTATO STAY 100% PROCEDURAL (adopt brief 3's isMobileGPU gate over brief 1's mobile-LOD GLBs). VERIFIED isMobileGPU() exists (mobilePerf, imported line 21). Gate all three loadModel calls behind if(!isMobileGPU()). Rationale: the fidelity delta is only legible at desktop resolution/distance; mobile keeps the byte-identical merged path, so mobile draw-call delta = +0 and mobile GPU memory delta = 0. This makes the whole workstream provably safe for the iOS/WKWebView 60fps seal and the 15s adaptive-governor warmup with NO mobile-side risk surface.
- AO IS BAKED INTO THE GLB, NOT RE-POINTED. Exception to the zero-texture rule: each GLB embeds ONE small AO map on UV0 (aoMap.channel=0 is hardcoded in assetLoader). The re-pointed terracotta/travertine sets carry diff/normal/rough tiling; the baked AO carries the deep contact shadow under the eave cornice, inside the bifora reveal, and in the coppo valleys — the primary depth cue where desktop SSAO does not reach the crown silhouette. This is the one place brief 1's bake discipline is non-negotiable.
- CAMPANILE APEX CLEARANCE IS A HARD BLENDER-SIDE CONSTRAINT. VERIFIED belfry math at lines 2967-2990: belfryY0=crownY+0.4, belfryH=3.4. Campanile topY=21, so belfry top ~24.9 before cupola/lantern; dome apex local ~27.7. Do NOT increase belfryH. Author campanile_cap.glb at exact world scale (1 Blender unit = 1 world unit), screenshot at a WP1/WP5-matched camera, and assert cupola+lantern apex Y stays below ~27.0 (0.7 clearance) BEFORE export, so the lantern never silhouettes above the dome in the reduced-motion stills.
- INSTANCE PER TYPE, SCALE PER TOWER. One tower_cap master authored at fp=6.0; InstancedMesh x5 with per-instance uniform scale = fp/6.0 (fp range 5.5-6.5) and matrix translate to (tx, topY, tz). One campanile_cap singleton at TOWERS[0] (-38,-24,topY=21). One bifora_window master, InstancedMesh on tower arrival (-Z) faces with +/-2% scale jitter for grown-over-centuries asymmetry. Never export N towers.
- ADD TO massGroup, NOT scene. VERIFIED massGroup.position.x=2 (line 3115), palace.add(massGroup) (3116). All TOWERS coords are in the pre-shift (x=-2 asymmetric) space; the massGroup +2 shift centres them. Set InstancedMesh matrices with raw TOWERS[i].tx/tz and call massGroup.add(...) so the centring is inherited free. scene.add would place towers 2 units east of the dome.
- COPPO TILES ARE REAL GEOMETRY, BAKED FLAT AT EXPORT. Author one coppo half-tube tile (SCREW lathe U-profile) instanced across the hip surface via Geometry Nodes instance-on-points with seed-stable rot/pos jitter, then APPLY+JOIN to one static mesh — zero Geo Nodes at runtime (brief 3). This is the single biggest silhouette win vs the current 6-triangle flat hipRoof, at ~350 tris per cap.
- NO GENERATIVE, NO SKETCHFAB, NO POLYHAVEN GEOMETRY. All masonry is deterministic scripted BPY (unanimous across briefs). Polyhaven allowed ONLY as an optional CC0 terracotta reference tint for the coppo bake; travertine/serena authored procedural (noise+voronoi) and baked. Hyper3D/Rodin/Hunyuan3D reserved for a future figural mascaron on the campanile keystone — explicitly OUT of WS03 scope.

**Assets:**
- **public/models/exterior/campanile_cap.glb** — Scripted BPY. West clock campanile crown as ONE unique GLB placed at TOWERS[0] (-38,-24, topY=21). Belfry pier-pilasters (4x box+bevel+cap), twin bifora per face (SCREW-lathe semicircle arches boolean-cut, central lathe colonnette), bronze bell (SCREW-lathe bell profile + spherical crown on a short yoke tucked behind piers — no floating headstock bar), 4 corner pinnacle spirelets (octagonal base + 4-sided cone + finial sphere+spike), octagonal drum (8-sided cyl), 8-panel coppo cupola (subdiv box squashed + coppo antefix ring via Geo-Nodes then applied), solid neck, lantern drum+ball+spike, and a pedimented clock aedicule on the -Z face (moulded panel, bronze bezel torus, pale travertine dial, 12 Roman-numeral markers + 2 hands BAKED to a 512px atlas — not runtime geometry, no font dependency). APEX MUST STAY < ~27.0 local. Bake NORMAL+AO+ROUGHNESS on Cycles GPU, sun #FFB870 at [-20,18,-30], exposure 1.0. · <=1300 tris desktop; DRACO L6 pos14 nrm10 uv12; <30KB compressed; <500KB ceiling easily met · No embedded diff/nor/rough — re-point stone slots to stoneTex(loadPlasterWallTextures) and coppo slots to roofTileTex(loadTerracottaTileTextures) post-load. Embeds ONE 512px baked AO on UV0. Micro-materials: bronze bell #8C6D42 (metal 0.85 rough 0.38, clearcoat desktop-only via mkPhys, kept as a separate named node so mkPhys traversal hits it), gold hands #B8973A, pale dial #F7F0E3 — as tiny embedded GLTF materials sharing no atlas UVs.
- **public/models/exterior/tower_cap.glb** — Scripted BPY. Shared coppo hip-roof cap for all 5 plain towers, authored at fp=6.0. Two-band stone eave cornice (2 square box rings fp+1.0 / fp+0.6); coppo hip-roof from ONE half-tube tile (SCREW lathe U-profile) instanced on the hip surface via Geometry Nodes instance-on-points with seed-stable rot/pos jitter, then APPLY+JOIN to one static mesh; antefix roll-tile ring at the eave (round(fp) 6-sided cyls rotated); finial stack (serena drum + travertine ball + thin spike). Two material slots (TRAVERTINE cornice/finial, TERRACOTTA coppo). Bake NORMAL+AO+ROUGHNESS; 2px cage; AO must darken the coppo valleys and the cornice underside. InstancedMesh x5 with per-instance scale = fp/6.0 (5.5-6.5). · <=600 tris desktop (~350 in the coppo field); DRACO L6; <20KB compressed · No embedded diff/nor/rough — re-point cornice/finial to stoneTex, coppo to roofTileTex. Embeds ONE 512px baked AO on UV0. Reuses the eager terracotta+travertine sets already in the scene, so zero new fetches, zero new eager slots.
- **public/models/exterior/bifora_window.glb** — Scripted BPY. Bifora window tile instanced on the -Z arrival faces of every tower (1 per tower at topY-2.1; a 2nd at topY-6.0 for towers with topY>16). BLOCKER FIX: ALSO capture the pre-branch double crown cornice lines 2953-2954 or the GLB eave z-fights it. ### WS04 — Monumental entrance stair + gold tympanum

*Grand travertine stair, pediment, gilded tympanum bearing the owner name (must stay dynamically re-drawable per user).*

**Summary:** WS04 ships 4 desktop-only scripted-bpy DRACO GLBs (Corinthian capital x6, palmette acroterion x3, carved tazza urn x2, volute-keystone door arch x1) gated behind a NEW flag3d('w3_exterior'), additive-swap over the retained procedural entrance cluster with silent fallback; the baluster GLB is DROPPED from first ship because procedural balusters are fused into the shared gTrimR merged draw call and cannot be removed without shattering it.
**Priority `P2` · ~4.5d · Feasible: yes · Confidence 0.82**

**Vision.** Replace the flattest, most-read primitives of the entrance cluster — the box-cap "capitals," cone "acroteria," stacked-cylinder urns, and the depthless pediment/tympanum slab — with a small kit of scripted-bpy DRACO GLBs that read as recognizable late-Renaissance Serena-order ornament at the WP3 tympanum beat (d=118, ~7.5s) and the WP5 door approach (d=63, ~15s), WITHOUT ever baking the owner's name and WITHOUT touching mobile/iOS geometry. The synthesis grafts: (1) the HYBRID brief's discipline of KEEPING every already-correct procedural system (crepidoma, column shafts+fluting, pediment triglyphs/dentils, stair treads, portal doors, and above all the dynamic Canvas name-decal) and replacing only the four highest-ROI details; (2) the PERF-FIRST brief's hard InstancedMesh-for-balusters lever, staggered idle-deferred loads to dodge the governor warmup window, and the explicit renderOrder/z-fight discipline; (3) the PHOTOREAL brief's proper classical grammar for the hero pieces (real acanthus capital, coffered/ribbed relief, volute keystone) — but sized to the HYBRID's ≤8k-tri, ≤1.2MB, ≤2-net-draw-call envelope rather than PHOTOREAL's 18k. The result: five focused assets, gated behind a fresh flag3d('w3_exterior'), desktop-only, additive-and-swap, with silent procedural fallback on any failure. The name stays a live CanvasTexture forever — non-negotiable across all three briefs and the routing doctrine.

**Design decisions:**
- FLAG: introduce flag3d('w3_exterior'); W3 = W2 && flag3d('w3_exterior'), read ONCE at scene mount (never per-frame). Staging ON / prod OFF automatically via existing PROD_HOSTS logic — no code change to flags3d.ts needed, the mechanism already resolves any named flag. No flag retirement until prod+iOS QA pass.
- SCOPE = REPLACE-ONLY-THE-WEAKEST (from HYBRID, rejecting PHOTOREAL's full stair/aedicula rebuild): KEEP procedural verbatim — the 3-step crepidoma, portico platform, all 6 column shafts+fluting, the pediment raking cornices/triglyphs/dentils/corona, the ShapeGeometry tympanum FILL, the 4-flight monumental stair treads, the portal void+architrave+doors+bronze rings, AND the Canvas name-decal. Rebuilding the whole stair (PHOTOREAL) buys little at d=63–118 for +12k tris and z-fight/offset risk against known-correct dimensions; not worth it.
- THE FOUR HERO REPLACEMENTS (HYBRID's targets, PHOTOREAL's grammar, PERF's budgets): (1) Corinthian capital tile placed 6x; (2) palmette acroterion placed 3x; (3) carved tazza urn placed 2x; (4) door transom arch + volute keystone placed 1x. PLUS (5) one lathe baluster as an InstancedMesh for the terrace/ramp guardrails — the single best draw-call win.
- BALUSTERS = InstancedMesh, NOT per-instance clones (PERF-FIRST winner, adopted over PHOTOREAL's 48 discrete placements only where it said InstancedMesh, and over any per-mesh export): author ONE baluster_master.glb (8-segment SCREW, ~96 tris), build a single THREE.InstancedMesh from its BufferGeometry, place along terrace/ramp cheeks reusing the existing baluX()/baluZ() position math with +/-5deg Y-jitter. 1 draw call regardless of count. This REPLACES the merged procedural cylinder balusters — net draw-call neutral or better.
- THE NAME DECAL IS UNTOUCHABLE (unanimous across all 3 briefs + routing doctrine): the drawTymName / CanvasTexture / namePlane flow (renderOrder=2, depthWrite:false, ~ (0, 8.28, vestZ-1.16)) is retained verbatim and stays procedural in the W2 block, overlaying both W2 and W3. No GLB carries letterforms — text is owner-dynamic, re-drawn on font-load and store hydration. W3 GLBs sit spatially AROUND the tympanum (capitals below at y~6.775, acroteria above at y~9.2/10.0), never in the namePlane's z-layer.
- DESKTOP-ONLY, HARD GUARD (HYBRID+PERF): wrap the entire W3 async block in if (W3 && !isMobileGPU()). On mobile/iOS/potato the flag resolves such that ALL five GLBs are skipped and the existing W2 procedural renders unchanged — ZERO mobile tri/draw-call/GPU-memory increase, so the iOS free-tier seal and the 750k/80-call/140MB binding ceiling are untouched by construction. This sidesteps the whole mobile-LOD authoring burden for WS04.
- INTEGRATION SEAM = async-after-sync-pass, swap-on-success, silent-fallback (all 3 briefs agree): inside the existing scene useEffect, AFTER the synchronous W2 geometry pass, a nested async IIFE (kept OUT of the namePlane closure to avoid double-registering the redraw ref). loadModel() each GLB, traverse+mkPhys() every material, then remove the procedural equivalents (box-caps, cones, cylinder-urns, procedural balusters, and hide transomMesh) and add the GLBs. try/catch → on reject, procedural stays visible. Dispose ONLY via clearModelCache() at unmount; never dispose clones.
- mkPhys() REAPPLY IS MANDATORY (unanimous risk callout — verified: modelLoader.ts line 29-34 sets only castShadow/receiveShadow, never mkPhys): after every loadModel().then(), traverse the group and call mkPhys() on each Mesh material, rebuilding color/roughness/metalness/normalMap/aoMapIntensity from canon. Author ONLY Principled BSDF (BaseColor/Metallic/Roughness/Normal) in Blender — no clearcoat/sheen/transmission (stripped on mobile, can leave broken slots on some drivers). Do NOT trust embedded GLB materials.
- STAGGERED IDLE-DEFERRED LOADS to dodge the governor (PERF-FIRST's sharpest lever): the adaptive governor demotes a tier for 7 days if >20% of frames miss 25ms in the first ~15s. Four+ concurrent DRACO decompressions on the main thread during the dolly would spike frame time. Defer the whole W3 block behind requestIdleCallback (or setTimeout 0) AFTER the first rendered frame, and load SEQUENTIALLY with a short chain (capital → acroterion → urn → door-arch → baluster), largest-first, so no two decodes overlap. Even though this is desktop-only, staggering keeps the establishing dolly buttery.
- Z-FIGHT / renderOrder DISCIPLINE (PERF+HYBRID): the door-arch GLB overlaps the existing transom CylinderGeometry — REMOVE/hide transomMesh before adding the GLB (do not layer). Author all GLB materials fully opaque (alphaTest=0, no transparency) so default renderOrder=0 sorts correctly BEHIND the renderOrder=2 name-decal. Read palace.matrixWorld for the true world Y of urn placements (centralGroup is offset to HILL_Y+0.3 AFTER scene.add) rather than hardcoding — the async load runs after positioning.
- MATERIAL BUDGET = ZERO net-new material families beyond 2 shared 512 PBR sets (HYBRID's byte-discipline): pietra_serena set shared by capital+acroterion+door-arch (albedo #7C8288, rough 0.72, metal 0); travertine_urn set for the urn (albedo #E8DCC0/TRAVERTINE canon, rough 0.65). Both authored PROCEDURAL in Blender (noise+voronoi veining, no scan exists — routing doctrine) and baked; NO Polyhaven geometry, Polyhaven only as optional albedo/rough base driver. AO baked to UV0 ONLY (assetLoader forces aoMap.channel=0 — select UV0 before bake so AO lands on channel 0, not UV1).
- REDUCED-MOTION STILLS CONTRACT (all 3): the three composed stills bracket WP1 (d~180), WP3 (d=118, theta=1.548pi, phi=0.306pi — the hero), WP5 (d~35). Every hero GLB must read correctly at exactly those three angles. Preview in the Blender viewport from the WP3 spherical camera (~ x=-40,y=25,z=-90 looking at origin) BEFORE export; verify capital silhouette, acroterion profile, urn proportion, and keystone read.

### WS05 — Facade walls: travertine + worn plaster

*Layered stucco-over-stone, patina, staining, quoins, pilasters, cornices — the dominant surface language.*

**Summary:** WS05 Le Sette Sorelle facade: upgrade the hoofdblok wall to a worn-limewash bake on a CLONED material (never the shared M.stone ramp) plus one scripted-bpy DRACO facade_kit.glb (quoins, string-courses, desktop-only pilasters/entablature) placed via InstancedMesh, all behind flag3d('w3_exterior') with sub-flags w3_intonaco/w3_facade_kit, additive-only over the procedural fallback.
**Priority `P1` · ~4d · Feasible: yes · Confidence 0.72**

**Vision.** Keep the procedural wall MASSING and the PLASTER_RAMP tone canon exactly as-is — the flat BoxGeometry walls are already correct in silhouette and colour at every dolly distance (nearest hero beat is WP3 at d=118, not a close-up). The perceived-quality gap at those distances is not surface texture, it is the total ABSENCE of three-dimensional stone relief that casts real shadows and divides the elevation. So WS05 is a HYBRID: (1) upgrade the wall's PBR texture set once to a true worn-limewash bake (the biggest textural jump for zero geometry, zero draw calls), and (2) add a single scripted-bpy 'facade_kit' relief language — rusticated quoins, a continuous cornicione/string-course band system, and entrance pilasters+entablature framing the tympanum name-beat — placed by InstancedMesh and merged-per-material so it costs almost nothing on the draw-call budget that actually binds mobile. This is the Hybrid brief's core judgment, hardened with the Perf-First brief's binding-budget discipline and the Photoreal brief's differential-patina instanceColor pass. All new code is additive-only behind flag3d('w3_exterior'); the procedural geometry stays in the scene as the guaranteed fallback if any GLB or texture load rejects.

**Design decisions:**
- REJECT full wall-panel GLB replacement (Photoreal + Perf-First briefs both authored new flat 'facade panel' meshes). The procedural BoxGeometry walls already provide correct massing at zero tri cost and are the safe fallback. Replacing them adds tris and draw calls for a surface that reads fine at d=118. Adopt the Hybrid brief's 'keep procedural walls, add relief only' stance. Net wall-geometry change: zero.
- KEEP the PLASTER_RAMP 5-step tone canon (M.stone/stoneL/stoneW/stoneD/stoneDk). Do NOT swap the whole ramp. Under W3, upgrade only the base DIFFUSE/NORMAL/ROUGH/AO *textures* driving M.stone/M.stoneW on the hoofdblok to a true worn-limewash bake (worn_intonaco set), leaving towers/gallery on the existing painted-plaster read so patina VARIES across the corps ('cresciuto nei secoli'). Darker slots (stoneD/stoneDk) stay on clayPlaster — their grittier read is already correct.
- TEXTURE BUDGET: the worn_intonaco set REPLACES the paintedPlaster slot on the hoofdblok (same repeat, same material slot) rather than adding a 5th eager set — mobile maxEagerTextureSets=4 must not be pierced. Verified: getQuality().maxEagerTextureSets=4 on mobile, 2 on potato. Ship worn_intonaco_{diff|nor_gl|rough|ao}_1k.jpg + _512 variants (potato uses 512 via textureRes='512', 404→1k fallback already wired in loadJPGBase).
- RELIEF is ONE facade_kit.glb authored by scripted bpy (no generative AI, no Polyhaven/Sketchfab geometry), with named sub-meshes: quoin_strip (~160 tris), string_course_seg (swept cyma/cavetto/corona profile), plinth_course_seg, win_architrave_seg, pilaster_l / pilaster_r + entrance frieze block. One shared travertine PBR atlas. This is the union of all three briefs' geometry lists, deduplicated and merged into a single small GLB (~30-60KB DRACO).
- INSTANCING + LOD tiering: quoins = 1 InstancedMesh (8 corners desktop / 4 front corners mobile). String-course = merged per height-band, 4 bands desktop / 2 bands (base+roofline) mobile. Pilasters + entablature = DESKTOP ONLY (not readable at d>=80 on mobile viewport) — this is the Perf-First brief's cut, adopted. Window architraves = desktop only. Net new draw calls: ~6 desktop, ~2 mobile, 0 potato.
- GLB MATERIALS: modelLoader.loadModel returns GLTFLoader materials (MeshStandardMaterial) that BYPASS loadPBRSet. Verified two seam requirements: (a) explicitly set mat.aoMap.channel=0 + needsUpdate in the post-load traverse (GLTFLoader defaults aoMap to channel 1 / uv2 → baked AO silently invisible on mobile otherwise); (b) mkPhys(THREE,props) CONSTRUCTS a new material from props — it does not mutate — so re-apply the canon by rebuilding each kit material via mkPhys with the shared travertine maps (envMapIntensity 0.65 to match M.stone, roughness ~0.52, metalness 0, aoMapIntensity 0.55–0.8). Do not just call mkPhys on the existing instance.
- DIFFERENTIAL PATINA via InstancedMesh.setColorAt (Photoreal brief), NOT vertexColors on shared geometry (that API multiplies material.color and conflicts with the shared PBR map). Lower instances (y<4) → PLASTER_RAMP.dark tint, mid → base, top (y>8) → light. instanceColor multiplies the sampled albedo — set material.color=white. Sells 'sun-bleached top / stain-dark base' at zero texture cost.
- DEFER the GLB load until AFTER onReady() fires (scene stable), not inside the initial useEffect setup. Verified onReady fires on first frame (~line 4844). The 18s dolly warmup is exactly when the adaptive governor samples frame deltas; a DRACO parse spike during 2.5–17.5s could trigger a false demotion. loadModel is async + cached; wrap in try/catch so reject leaves procedural geometry intact.
- FLAG: W3 = W2 && flag3d('w3_exterior') read once at mount. Verified flag3d('w3_exterior') works with the existing sessionStorage/?flag3d mechanism with zero flags3d.ts change (staging ON / prod OFF). Optional per-feature sub-flags w3_intonaco (all tiers) and w3_facade_kit (relief GLB) for isolated QA rollback. No flag retirement until iOS WKWebView + potato verified.
- Z-FIGHTING: offset every relief mesh +0.005 outward from the wall face IN BLENDER before export (string-course sits coplanar with the wall box face otherwise). Quoins sit at x=±(halfWidth+0.08) proud of the wall — safe against the 2.5 near plane. Do NOT lower the near plane to 'fix' depth artifacts (worsens distant-terrain precision). Verify at min user zoom.
- TEXTURE SOURCING: worn_intonaco bake starts from Polyhaven CC0 (beige_wall_001 base diff + weathered_concrete normal blended ~0.35 for micro-cracking) composited + stain-masked in Blender, then colour-clamped to PLASTER_RAMP.base (#F2E9DA family, ≤0.6 rel-luminance) before export so it stays canon-compliant. Travertine trim atlas is fully PROCEDURAL (Voronoi+Noise veining, #E8DCC0) baked — no scan matches travertine. Polyhaven supplies TEXTURE only, never geometry.

Adds 0 draw calls. - Zero change to modelLoader.ts, flags3d.ts, canon.ts. Only ExteriorScene.tsx (seam) + assetLoader.ts (two wrappers) change.
- Dispose only at unmount via clearModelCache(); never dispose clones returned by loadModel.

**LOD tiers:**
- Desktop (full): worn_intonaco walls + full facade_kit — 8 quoins, 4 string-course bands, pilasters+entablature framing WP3 name-beat, window architraves, differential-patina instanceColor.
- Mobile/iOS (reduced): worn_intonaco walls + reduced facade_kit — 4 front-corner quoins, 2 string-course bands (base + roofline). NO pilasters/architraves/extra bands (guarded by if(!isMobileQ)).
- Potato (minimal): worn_intonaco optionally at 512 + facade_kit SKIPPED entirely (procedural BoxGeometry walls only, no shadows, no env map). Baked AO channel 0 carries contact shadow where SSAO is off.
- No distance-LOD needed: relief reads at the fixed dolly distances (nearest hero beat WP3 d=118); a single mobile LOD authored <=750k governs both mobile and potato geometry.

**Dependencies:** Blocks on: read of ExteriorScene.tsx W2 block (~300–1400) to enumerate hoofdblok-specific mk() calls before the material clone can be scoped correctly (feasibility blocker #1)., Depends on modelLoader.loadModel (unchanged), /public/draco/ decoder (warm), assetLoader loadPBRSet contract (unchanged; two additive wrappers)., Independent of WS other-workstreams for correctness, but SHARES the facade_travertine atlas (Slot B) — coordinate so WS covering balustrades/urns/cornices reuse the SAME travertine set to stay under the mobile eager-texture cap (maxEagerTextureSets=4 mobile / 2 potato)., KTX2 fast-follow (npm run build:ktx2, needs toktx) is non-blocking; manifest feature-detect + per-file JPG fallback already wired., Owner pre-req: confirm Cycles GPU (HIP) bake enabled in Blender N-panel; confirm Polyhaven enabled.

**Feasibility:**
- Perf risk: low
- iOS risk: low
- Blender MCP can produce: yes
- Blocker: Shared-material blocker: worn_intonaco swap on M.stone/M.stoneW repaints the whole corps, defeating the varied-patina goal — must split the hoofdblok material first (see requiredFixes[0]). This is the single load-bearing correctness issue; the plan flagged it as an open question but shipped the swap as if scoped to the hoofdblok.
- Blocker: Missing-texture-set 404 has no fallback to paintedPlaster (see requiredFixes[1]) — the intonaco swap is not covered by the try/catch safety the plan relies on.
- Fix: MATERIAL SHARING (plan's own open-Q1, now RESOLVED against code as a hard blocker): M.stone/stoneL/stoneW/stoneD/stoneDk (ExteriorScene.tsx:347-351) are ONE shared 5-step ramp used by the WHOLE corps — 87 M.stone* usages incl. hoofdblok (688), east gallery (892), ochreWall=M.stone (936), podia (1044). Swapping the base map on M.stone/M.stoneW to worn_intonaco repaints the ENTIRE villa, so the plan's 'varied patina — towers/gallery stay on old plaster' intent is impossible via a slot-swap. FIX: under W3, clone M.stone into a NEW material (e.g. M.stoneHoofdblok) applied only to the hoofdblok wall geometry, and swap the texture on the clone — do NOT mutate the shared M.stone. This requires re-pointing the specific hoofdblok mk() calls, not a one-line map assignment.
- Fix: TEXTURE 404 has NO graceful fallback for a MISSING set: loadPBRSet's 404 handling (assetLoader.ts:541) only degrades a resolution suffix (512/2k -> existing 1k) of an existing set. If worn_intonaco_*.jpg files are absent, the 1k fetch hard-404s and the wall renders untextured — the plan's 'procedural fallback' guarantee only covers the relief GLB (loadModel try/catch), NOT the intonaco texture swap. FIX: guard the intonaco swap behind an existence check or a sub-flag (w3_intonaco) and only repoint the map once the files are confirmed present; keep paintedPlasterTex as the assigned default.
- Fix: GLTFLoader materials bypass the hardcoded aoMap.channel=0 (which lives INSIDE loadPBRSet at assetLoader.ts:554, not in modelLoader). Confirmed: modelLoader.loadModel does NO channel fixup. The plan correctly requires manually setting mat.aoMap.channel=0 + needsUpdate in the post-load traverse for facade_kit.glb — this is mandatory or baked AO is silently invisible on mobile/potato. Keep it in the acceptance gate.
- Fix: mkPhys returns MeshPhysicalMaterial on desktop, MeshStandardMaterial on mobile (mobilePerf.ts:343-366) and CONSTRUCTS a new material from props (does not mutate) — plan's claim verified. Ensure the kit-material rebuild passes the shared travertine maps INTO mkPhys props (map/normalMap/roughnessMap/aoMap) rather than calling mkPhys on the loaded instance, else the canon is not applied.
- Fix: Add the dev-overlay assertion gate the plan promises but the codebase does not yet enforce: renderer.info.render.calls delta <=6 desktop / <=2 mobile, triangles delta <=4k mobile, and aoMap.channel===0 on every loaded kit material — verify on the Vercel preview with ?flag3d=w3_exterior on a real iOS WKWebView through the full 18s dolly before npx vercel --prod.
- Fix: DEFER the facade_kit.glb load until AFTER onReady fires (verified first-frame at ExteriorScene.tsx:4844) so the DRACO parse spike lands outside the 2.5-17.5s governor sampling window that triggers the 7-day tier demotion. The intonaco texture swap, by contrast, should happen synchronously in the geometry pass (it only changes an existing material slot, no parse spike).

### WS06 — Windows: arched, mullioned, shuttered

*Aediculae, mullions, glazing with believable reflections/refraction, wooden shutters, iron grilles.*

**Summary:** WS06 Aedicule Kit: two Blender-scripted DRACO GLB masters (a curved 12x drum thermal-bay wrapping the round r=8.2 W2 drum, plus an 11x central-block aedicule) instanced into ExteriorScene behind flag3d('w3_exterior'), replacing ONLY the ~200 loose centralGroup addArchedWindow draw calls while leaving richWindow merged block windows and the dead octagon/wing sites untouched — a large NET draw-call reduction at ~1000x fidelity.
**Priority `P1` · ~6d · Feasible: yes · Confidence 0.72**

**Vision.** Replace every flat-box/scatter-Mesh window on the villa with a small family of Blender-scripted aedicule tiles — deep stone reveals, moulded jambs, volute keystones, real-section mullions, thermal-bay drum oculi, and open louvred shutters — authored as GLB masters and placed at runtime via THREE.InstancedMesh so fidelity goes up ~1000x while draw calls go DOWN. This is a HYBRID synthesis that grafts the perf-first brief's core insight (windows are the #1 un-merged draw-call leak; each addArchedWindow fires ~18 Meshes and each richWindow more, across ~50-114 openings — instancing is a net WIN, not a cost) onto the photoreal brief's fidelity targets (full aedicule surround + entablature drum bays at the WP3 tympanum beat) and the hybrid brief's discipline (procedural path stays 100% intact as fallback; zero new runtime loader code). The single highest-ROI frame is WP3 (d=118, name-beat): drum thermal bays + main-block piano-nobile aediculae must read best dead-on at 6-30deg. Every hero tile must also compose correctly at the reduced-motion stills WP1/WP3/WP5. The design is deliberately tier-scaled: desktop gets the full kit, mobile gets a stripped LOD of the SAME masters (drum + main-block only), potato renders zero GLBs (existing procedural path untouched).

**Design decisions:**
- TIER SELECTOR CORRECTION (load-bearing, all three briefs got this wrong): getQuality().textureRes is '1k' on BOTH desktop and mobile — only potato is '512'. So `Q.textureRes==='512' ? lo : hi` selects the LO mesh on DESKTOP too. Wrong. Use getGPUTier() directly: tier==='desktop' -> hi LOD + full kit; tier==='mobile' -> lo LOD + drum/main-block subset; tier==='potato' -> zero GLBs (procedural fallback). Cache `const tier = getGPUTier()` once at mount before any await (dodges a mid-load governor demotion race).
- GATE = W3 && tier!=='potato'. Add `const W3 = W2 && flag3d('w3_exterior')` at the scene useEffect top (flags3d.ts needs NO change — w3_exterior auto-resolves staging-ON/prod-OFF). The explicit tier guard is separate from the flag so a future flag misconfig can never push GLB loads onto potato/iOS-jetsam-risk devices.
- SUPPRESS-not-augment under W3: wrap the existing addArchedWindow() call sites (lines 1087-1100, 2086, 2144, 2177, 2196-2197) and the richWindow() call sites (lines 2752, 2858) and the 8 drum disc stickers (lines 789-793) in `if (!W3) { ... }`. W3 REPLACES procedural windows; it never draws on top of them. This is the ONLY edit to the synchronous geometry pass, keeping the mobile/potato draw-call delta at exactly zero. If the async GLB load rejects, the catch re-runs the procedural helpers (or, simpler and safer: leave procedural drawn and skip the instancer on reject) — prod never sees an empty facade.
- ONE master GLB per window TYPE, never per instance. Three masters: aedicule_main.glb (piano-nobile + gallery + torri openings — the richWindow/addArchedWindow replacement), drum_thermal_bay.glb (Diocletian tripartite bay for the 8 drum faces — highest ROI at WP3), and (folded into aedicule_main as named submeshes, not a 4th file) the glass/shutter parts. Each master carries a 'hi' and a 'lo' named mesh so one file serves desktop and mobile.
- INSTANCING via named-submesh extraction: on load, traverse the Group, collect geometry per material slot (stone / glass / shutter), build ONE InstancedMesh per slot fed the same matrix array. Net draw-call delta: +3 desktop (stone IM + shutter IM + glass IM), +2 mobile (no shutter-detail bucket / iron omitted). This REPLACES ~50-114 openings * ~18 scatter meshes. Massive net reduction on the mobile 80-opaque-call ceiling.
- GLASS stays the SHARED existing M.win material reference (line 368) — do NOT clone it, or Three.js R166 transparent batching breaks and 50-114 glass quads become 50-114 draw calls. If per-facade merge is ever needed, merge glass quads per material before Mesh creation. Set depthWrite:false + renderOrder:1 on glass (matches the water/stain-decal pattern already in the codebase) to keep transparent sort cheap on A15 WKWebView.
- SHUTTER-hinge instancing: shutters open ~32deg on a hinge at their vertical EDGE, not center. InstancedMesh can't rotate around a per-instance local pivot cleanly, so author the shutter mesh in Blender with its ORIGIN AT the hinge edge; then the instance matrix = translate-to-hinge-world -> rotate 32deg about world-up -> place. Two shutters per opening = two instance sets (left mirrored). Reduced-motion: shutters render static at 32deg open (no animation). Desktop-with-motion optional: lerp 0->32deg over 800ms touching ONLY the shutter InstancedMesh.instanceMatrix, then set a done-flag and STOP updating (never burn 0.3ms/frame forever alongside grass/wheat uniforms).
- MATERIAL contract: exactly ONE new shared stone PBR set 'stone_aedicule' for all surround/keystone/sill geometry across all three masters. Glass reuses M.win. Shutters reuse woodDoorTex (already loaded, line 282) via the existing shutterMat pattern (line 944). Iron grate is DESKTOP-ONLY and reuses the existing ironMat (line 2422) — no new metal set. Net new texture upload: 4 files (one 1k PBR set), and even that loads INSIDE the async GLB block (after load succeeds), NOT in the synchronous allTexSets array (line 294) — this defers it past the mobile maxEagerTextureSets=4 cap so we never need owner sign-off to raise it.
- mkPhys() rebuild helper (not traverse-reassign): mkPhys NEWs a material and strips transmission/clearcoat on mobile — it does not mutate. GLTFLoader hands back MeshStandardMaterial. So write applyPhysical(mesh, extraProps) that READS the loaded material's {color,roughness,metalness,map,normalMap,aoMap,emissive} then calls mkPhys(THREE,{...extracted, clearcoat:0.1 (desktop-only, auto-stripped mobile)}) and reassigns. Call it on every traversed mesh material before building InstancedMeshes.
- UV0-ONLY export: assetLoader hardcodes aoMap.channel=0. Smart Project writes UV0 by default, but DELETE any auto-generated lightmap/second UV set in Blender before export or the baked AO lands on channel 1 and silently doesn't apply. Single UV set per master.
- DRACO only, never meshopt (no MeshoptDecoder registered — silent fail). Level 6, pos 14, nrm 10, uv 12; export_apply=True, export_yup=True, GLB. Assert header magic 0x46546C67 v2 with extensionsUsed containing KHR_draco_mesh_compression at export time. DRACO decoder is already warm from the two bust GLBs.
- DISPOSE discipline: push each InstancedMesh.material and .geometry to the existing extraDisposables path (mirror line 4924) at unmount. NEVER call clearModelCache() in the useEffect return — the bust GLBs share that cache. Store the built InstancedMeshes in local refs for cleanup.
- GOVERNOR-safe warmup: start the GLB fetch AFTER the first frame renders (async IIFE fires post synchronous pass) AND ideally after GOV_WARMUP_MS(2500ms), so DRACO CPU-decode jank doesn't land inside the governor's bad-window sampling and trigger a spurious desktop->mobile demotion. The 18s cinematic dolly gives ample buffer.

**Assets:**
- **public/models/exterior/aedicule_main.glb** — Scripted bpy (no generative AI). CURVE moulding profile (fillet+ovolo+cavetto) swept via SCREW+ARRAY along the opening rectangle; BOOLEAN DIFFERENCE into a wall slab for the >=0.35m reveal; TorusBevel half-circle arch ring (16 seg); SCREW-on-Bezier-S volute keystone; ARRAY box mullion bars (tripartite: 2 vertical + 1 transom); SCREW classical-scroll console corbels under a chamfered sill; louvred shutter = ARRAY of blade boxes, origin placed AT hinge edge. Hi-poly (~8k tris, subdiv mouldings) baked selected-to-active (cage 0.02m) onto low-poly. Two named meshes exported: 'aedicule_hi' + 'aedicule_lo'. Glass submesh 'glass' (flat quad + arch half-disc, no UVs, runtime M.win). Shutter submesh 'shutter' (reuses woodDoorTex). Iron grate submesh 'grate' (desktop-only, reuses ironMat). · hi ~420 tris/opening, lo ~140 tris/opening. Instanced ~50 (mobile: main-block+drum) to ~114 (desktop: all facades). Well under mobile 60k decorative-tri budget. · stone_aedicule set (shared). glass=M.win (no tex). shutter=woodDoorTex (existing). grate=ironMat (existing).
- **public/models/exterior/drum_thermal_bay.glb** — Scripted bpy. One flat pie-slice panel matching a 45deg octagon face (bDrumR=5, bDrumH=4 confirmed in code — 8 flat faces, no curvature fitting). Diocletian/thermal window: tripartite arched opening (two round-headed lights flanking a larger central light within one semicircular common arch), SCREW-swept jamb mouldings, pilaster-flanked aedicule (SCREW lathe shafts ~60 tris each), full entablature cyma-recta cornice on top, volute keystone, optional shell-hooded blind niches (hi only). VERIFY in Blender that pilaster+cornice radial protrusion does NOT collide with the dome base sphere before export (overlay drum + dome geometry). Bake normal+AO, cage 0.02m. · hi ~1200 tris/panel x8 = ~9.6k desktop; lo (niches stripped) ~380 tris/panel x8 = ~3k mobile. Single highest perceived-quality ROI at WP3 d=118. · stone_aedicule set (shared with aedicule_main). glass fill = M.win.

- Suppression is surgical: wrap ONLY lines 1087-1100 (11 centralGroup addArchedWindow openings, ~200 loose mk() draw calls) in `if(!W3)`. - Perf risk: low
- iOS risk: low
- Blender MCP can produce: yes
- Blocker: Drum asset targets non-W2 dead code (bDrumR=5 octagon / disc stickers 789-793 never render under the shipping W2 flag); the real W2 drum is a round 32-seg cylinder r=8.2 with a 12-window ring — the thermal-bay tile must be re-authored as a curved 12x panel.
- Blocker: Draw-call ROI premise is overstated ~4.5x: only the 11 centralGroup addArchedWindow openings (~200 loose calls) are an actual W2 leak; the wing addArchedWindow sites are dead under !W2 and the richWindow block windows are already merged into the static draw calls.

- Fix: RE-TARGET THE DRUM ASSET — the plan's drum_thermal_bay.glb is authored against DEAD CODE. The ACTUAL W2 drum (line 1748+) is a ROUND 32-segment cylinder, rDrumR=8.2, rDrumH=11.0, with 12 pilasters + 12 flat box 'windows' (M.win, 1.05x2.9) placed radially at 12 angles (lines 1776-1789). So the thermal-bay tile must be a CURVED panel wrapping a round cylinder r=8.2 and instanced 12x (not a flat pie-slice x8) — exactly the curvature-fit the plan explicitly dismissed. Re-author against lines 1748-1789 and delete every reference to bDrumR=5 / lines 789-793.
- Fix: FIX THE DRAW-CALL ARITHMETIC — the '~50-114 openings x ~18 meshes = 900+ draw calls' premise is false for W2. Verified the two window systems: (a) `addArchedWindow` (line 946, ~18 loose mk() meshes) is called on WINGS at 2086/2144/2177/2196 but that entire `wingDefs.forEach` block is guarded `if (!W2)` (line 1986) — DEAD under W2. (b) `richWindow` (line 2524) is the W2 window system and it emits via `box()` into merge buckets (gWallD/gWall/gWinM) that get mergeGeometries'd into the ~18 static draw calls at line 3131 — so richWindow windows already cost ~0 incremental draw calls. The ONLY genuine unmerged leak reachable under W2 is `addArchedWindow` on `centralGroup` at 1087-1100 = 11 openings (2 front + 3 back + 6 side) x ~18 meshes ≈ ~200 loose draw calls, NOT 900+. Real ROI is ~200 central draw calls collapsed to +3, plus fidelity — still a net win, but re-scope the claim and suppress ONLY 1087-1100 (not the dead 2086/2144/2177/2196/2752/2858 sites, which need no `if(!W3)` wrap).
- Fix: DROP OR RE-TARGET THE richWindow SUPPRESSION — the plan wraps richWindow sites (2752, 2858) in `if(!W3)`, but replacing richWindow means REMOVING geometry that is currently MERGED into the static draw calls and re-adding it as InstancedMesh. That converts ~0-cost merged geometry into +N instanced draw calls — a net draw-call REGRESSION on the blocks, the opposite of the plan's thesis. Recommend: leave richWindow (merged block windows) fully intact under W3 and only instance-replace the centralGroup addArchedWindow openings + the drum ring. This shrinks scope and removes the regression risk.
- Fix: REMOVE `clearcoat` FROM applyPhysical — verified mkPhys strips clearcoat on mobile but KEEPS it on desktop (mobilePerf.ts 343-345). The plan's applyPhysical injects `clearcoat:0.1` on loaded stone. Stone should be matte (canon: TRAVERTINE roughness ~0.72, envMapIntensity ~0.3). Adding desktop clearcoat to travertine surrounds will make them read as wet/varnished and clash with the merged procedural M.trim stone right next to them. Author flat MeshStandard, no clearcoat.
- Fix: GLASS-MATERIAL REUSE IS INCOMPATIBLE WITH INSTANCING AS DESCRIBED — the plan says reuse the shared `M.win` reference for the glass InstancedMesh AND says M.win must not be cloned. But M.win is a MeshPhysicalMaterial with transmission:0.6/ior:1.52 (line 368) on desktop; transmission on an InstancedMesh with 11+ instances and depthWrite:false is a known heavy transparent path. Verified M.win already carries transmission. Recommend: for the instanced glass, build ONE new shared MeshStandard glass (opacity-based, no transmission, matching mkPhys's mobile fallback) rather than reusing the transmission-heavy M.win — and confirm it in the extraDisposables cleanup. This is a divergence from the plan's 'reuse M.win' decision that the plan got backwards.
- Fix: VERIFY THE 60fps CLAIM EMPIRICALLY BEFORE PROD — perfAssert.ts already logs `renderer.info.render.calls` against a 150 mobile budget (confirmed). The net delta of the corrected scope (+~3 IM calls, -~200 loose calls, +1 PBR set ~4MB) is comfortably inside all ceilings, and the governor warmup deferral is sound. But the claim is unproven until measured inside iOS WKWebView during the 15s governor window. Gate prod-promote on an on-device capture showing calls DOWN and no governor demotion in the first 15s.

This is the highest-regression-risk edit (touches prod fallback). Do it as a standalone no-op refactor (procedural still consumes the const, visually diffed) BEFORE any GLB work.

### WS07 — Portico / loggia / arcades

*Column orders, arcaded galleries (the "galerij"), vaulted soffits, rhythm and shadow.*

**Summary:** WS07 — one Blender-authored modular travertine arcade kit (Tuscan column, 3-member archivolt, Corinthian capital, entablature, desktop-only coffered soffit) that REPLACES the real W2 wing-portico mk() meshes at ExteriorScene.tsx L2088-2137 via runtime InstancedMesh, reusing the EXISTING /textures/pbr/travertine atlas, gated behind flag3d('w3_exterior').
**Priority `P1` · ~9d · Feasible: yes · Confidence 0.82**

**Vision.** Replace the three flat procedural arcade systems (east-galerij loggia, cortile peristyle, and the entrance vestibulum's box-cap columns) with ONE tightly-scoped, Blender-authored modular stone kit that reads as a single villa "grown over centuries." The perceived-quality jump comes from three things the procedural version physically cannot do: (1) real classical PROFILES — 3-member archivolts, echinus/abacus and acanthus capitals, attic bases with torus/scotia — modeled once and baked; (2) DEPTH SHADOW that survives on mobile — coffered soffits/intrados whose recession is carried entirely by baked AO on UV0, because SSAO is desktop-only; (3) RHYTHM — genuine arch reveals casting long SW-sun shadows at the golden hour, dead-on at the WP3 tympanum name-beat (d=118) which is the single most-read frame.

The organizing principle that resolves every tradeoff between the three competing briefs is INSTANCE-THE-REPEATS, MERGE-THE-UNIQUES, REPLACE-NEVER-ADD, and SHARE-ONE-STONE-ATLAS. The photoreal brief's classical correctness (full archivolt members, cassettoni, acanthus) is kept but demoted to a desktop-only HI mesh baked down onto a shared LO game mesh. The perf-first brief's InstancedMesh discipline and REPLACE-not-ADD draw-call accounting is the binding law. The hybrid brief's insight — that the loggia today has NO soffit and the eye sees straight through to sky, reading as a stage-flat — is adopted as the #1 desktop win, but gated so mobile spends zero tris on it.

Everything is gated behind a fresh flag3d('w3_exterior') (staging ON / prod OFF automatically, no code change needed — the flag mechanism already defaults non-prod-hosts to true). W3 = W2 && flag3d('w3_exterior'), read ONCE at mount. GLBs load ASYNC after the synchronous W2 geometry pass; the procedural fallback is never removed until the GLB resolves cleanly, so any reject/timeout silently keeps today's scene. Proven at 60fps inside iOS WKWebView via the dev renderer.info overlay before any prod promote.

**Design decisions:**
- SINGLE SHARED STONE ATLAS, not per-system textures. All kit pieces reference ONE PBR set: public/textures/pbr/arcade_stone/ with the canonical {prefix}_{diff|nor_gl|rough|ao}_1k.jpg naming that loadPBRSet already expects. Albedo target TRAVERTINE #E8DCC0, roughness ~0.72, no metalness. Reason: the mobile eager-texture cap is 4 sets (maxEagerTextureSets=4 in mobilePerf.ts, verified); three separate arcade texture sets would blow it. One set = one GPU texture slot shared by galerij + peristyle + vestibulum. It must also SHARE with the WS05 baluster and WS06 fountain sets (all travertine) so the whole stone family is one atlas.
- INSTANCE THE REPEATS, MERGE THE UNIQUES. Every repeated element (column unit, arch bay, entablature tile, soffit panel) is authored ONCE in Blender and placed at runtime as THREE.InstancedMesh (1 draw call each), NOT exported as 7 baked copies. Placement matrices are computed in TypeScript from the SAME bay-spacing math the current procedural loop already uses (verified at ExteriorScene.tsx line ~711: `ax` column stride and `-(pzD/2-0.1)` z-plane). This is the perf-first brief's rule and it is non-negotiable; the photoreal brief's 'ARRAY 7 bays into one GLB' is REJECTED for the loggia because a pre-arrayed 7-bay GLB is 7x the download and can't LOD per-distance. Exception: the entablature/cornice run and the back-cap spandrel wall ARE merged (they are continuous, not repeated units).
- REPLACE, NEVER ADD — net draw-call delta must be <= 0 on every tier. On the W3 path the procedural loggia meshes (the 7 CylinderGeometry columns + BoxGeometry caps + TorusGeometry arches at ExteriorScene.tsx ~line 711-719) are tagged userData.ws07=true BEFORE the async load, and scene-removed ONLY after the GLB InstancedMesh resolves cleanly. Peristyle and vestibulum same pattern. Verified draw-call arithmetic: loggia -~13 procedural +2 instanced = -11; vestibulum capitals -12 box prims +1 instanced(6 clones) = -11; peristyle desktop-only. Net exterior draw-call REDUCTION, buying headroom for other WS.
- TWO LOD MESHES PER PIECE, TOGGLED BY .visible — not a LOD framework. Each GLB carries a named HI mesh and LO mesh (naming convention COLUMN_HI / COLUMN_LO etc.). Desktop instances the HI; mobile/potato instances the LO. This mirrors the existing grass-instance visibility-toggle pattern already in the codebase. Distance-LOD for the 18s dolly is a simple .visible swap at camera distance thresholds — both InstancedMeshes pre-built, zero re-load.
- MOBILE SKIPS THE PERISTYLE AND THE SOFFITS ENTIRELY. The cortile peristyle is interior-courtyard and never the hero silhouette from any waypoint; it is desktop-only (gated behind !isMobileGPU()). The coffered soffit/intrados HI detail is desktop-only too — mobile gets a flat baked-AO barrel soffit. Only the tiny vestibulum Corinthian capital (~320-tri LO) and the arch+column LO load on mobile, because the vestibulum face is the WP3 name-beat hero. This keeps mobile within the 60k-tri / 15-GLB-draw-call decorative budget with room to spare.
- mkPhys MUST BE RE-APPLIED after every loadModel. Verified: modelLoader.loadModel only sets castShadow/receiveShadow — it does NOT run mkPhys, so GLTFLoader's raw MeshStandardMaterial (or a Physical export) survives untouched. A dedicated helper applyArcadeMaterials(group, THREE, arcadeSet) traverses every Mesh, rebuilds material via mkPhys(THREE, {map,normalMap,roughnessMap,aoMap, color:'#E8DCC0', roughness:0.72, metalness:0}) — which auto-downgrades Physical→Standard on mobile — and sets aoMap.channel=0 (matches the hardcoded assetLoader contract, verified line 554). Author STANDARD PBR only; no clearcoat/sheen/transmission (stripped on mobile anyway).
- VESTIBULUM CAPITAL SLOTS ONTO EXISTING SHAFTS — no shaft geometry change. The Corinthian capital GLB abacus matches the existing serenaOrder box-cap footprint (1.4x0.3x1.4) exactly and clones onto the 6 existing procedural shafts at their current cx/vestZ. Desktop only for the full acanthus; mobile ships a 320-tri baked LO (raise to 640 if the leaf silhouette blobs). This is the single highest perceived-quality target because the vestibulum reads dead-on at WP3.
- DRACO LEVEL 6 EXPORT, NEVER MESHOPT. Verified: modelLoader registers DRACOLoader (decoder at /draco/) and NO MeshoptDecoder — a meshopt GLB fails silently. Export params: draco level 6, pos 14, nrm 10, uv 12, export_apply=True, export_yup=True, export_tangents=True (so Three doesn't recompute and flip the OpenGL normal), WEBP embedded. Build-time assert: GLB magic 0x46546C67, v2, extensionsUsed contains KHR_draco_mesh_compression; fail the build otherwise. The two bust GLBs already warm the DRACO worker on every exterior mount, so the arcade GLBs (arriving >2.5s in, after the synchronous pass) decode without a cold-start stall inside the governor's 15s window.
- BAKE TO MATCH THE ONE SUN / ONE GRADE. Bake AO into the ao channel on UV0 (SSAO is desktop-only so baked AO carries mobile/potato depth). Bake curvature/Pointiness into roughness (convex arch edges read lighter). Blend a 0.3x-weight directional-shadow bake from the canon sun — DirectionalLight #FFB870 at [-20,18,-30] (verified GOLDEN.sunPosition in canon.ts) — into the AO so the intrados carries the golden-hour rake even where dynamic shadows don't reach. Bake at exposure 1.0 (runtime applies EXPOSURE 1.15 NeutralToneMapping once). Normals OpenGL convention (Blender default). No gold/emissive on any arcade piece — stone stays <=0.6 rel-luminance so memories remain the brightest pixels.
- POLYHAVEN FOR TEXTURE DETAIL ONLY, NEVER GEOMETRY. Optionally blend a CC0 travertine/beige_wall normal (get_polyhaven_categories then search_polyhaven_assets 'travertine'/'beige wall' at 1k) as a 30% overlay into the Blender bake for mortar-joint variation — but the shipped normal/AO/rough are the BAKED outputs, not the Polyhaven files directly. The complete fallback if Polyhaven is unavailable is a pure procedural Voronoi+Noise stone material (ColorRamp #C8BC9E->#EADDC0->#F0E9D8) — no plan dependency on Polyhaven. Add any CC0 source to CREDITS.md.
- SEQUENCED, GUARDED INTEGRATION SEAM. Insert `const W3 = W2 && flag3d('w3_exterior');` at the line-98 flag block. In an async post-geometry block: HIDE (visible=false) the tagged procedural loggia/vestibulum meshes at the START of the async block to avoid a swap-flash, then Promise.all the loadModel calls, applyArcadeMaterials + build InstancedMeshes on success, then scene.remove the tagged procedural meshes and register GLB geo/materials in extraDisposables. On ANY reject: un-hide the procedural fallback, skip the instanced add, console.warn('[WS07] GLB load failed, keeping procedural'). clearModelCache() only at unmount; never dispose clones.

### WS08 — Balustrades + urns + finials

*The signature moodboard balustrade run with pinecone urns and finials; instanced along terraces and roofline.*

**Summary:** WS08 balustrade/urn/finial/coping kit — one DRACO GLB (geometry + UV0 only, no embedded textures) placed via InstancedMesh behind flag3d('w3_exterior'), driven by a shared travertine_ornament PBR set, REPLACING (not adding to) the procedural CylinderGeometry balusters and box-stack urns in ExteriorScene.tsx.
**Priority `P1` · ~3.5d · Feasible: yes · Confidence 0.78**

**Vision.** Retire the single ugliest tell in the whole exterior: the procedural CylinderGeometry baluster rows and box-stack "urns" that repeat across every terrace, parapet, stair-foot and roofline in ExteriorScene.tsx. Replace them with four scripted-bpy, DRACO-compressed GLB master modules — a lathe-turned vase-and-torus baluster, a pinecone garden urn on a chamfered plinth, a slender pinecone roofline finial, and a 1m mitre-cut travertine coping cap — placed at runtime via THREE.InstancedMesh so 400+ repeated pieces collapse to a handful of draw calls. This is the highest-ROI decorative group in WS08 because balustrades and their terminating urns read dead-on at all five cinematic waypoints and at the three reduced-motion stills (WP1/WP3/WP5): the perceived jump from "chunky stacked cylinders" to "honed travertine classical ornament" is enormous for a tiny, deterministic authoring cost. Everything is additive and flag-gated (W3 = W2 && flag3d('w3_exterior')): staging ON / prod OFF, iOS never touches it until QA-cleared in WKWebView, and on any reject the existing procedural geometry stays live with zero regression.

**Design decisions:**
- SYNTHESIS VERDICT: adopt the PERF-FIRST brief's tier/instancing spine and net-zero-draw-call discipline as the master frame; graft the PHOTOREAL brief's four-asset split (coping cap as a separate 4th module) and richer desktop profiles; take the HYBRID brief's Promise.allSettled parallel load, DRACO-decoder-warmup guard, and governor-demotion guard.
- TEXTURE DECISION: reject the HYBRID shortcut of reusing loadTravertineTextures(). Author a dedicated shared 'travertine_ornament' PBR set (verified path: assetLoader.ts:641 shows loadTravertineTextures already exists as the pattern to copy) so baked AO/normal carry the chisel + pinecone-scale relief that match the NEW geometry. But SHARE that one set across all four GLBs via a single loadPBRSet call and reuse the same THREE.Texture instances by reference — never per-GLB texture instances. This is the #1 iOS jetsam guard.
- LOD DECISION: two LODs authored per lathed asset (baluster/urn/finial) as separately-named meshes inside ONE kit GLB (baluster_lo/hi, urn_lo/hi, finial_lo/hi, coping). Pick lo vs hi at mount by getQuality().maxEagerTextureSets (<=4 => mobile geometry), NOT isMobileGPU() — this is the governor-demotion fix from the HYBRID brief, since a desktop demoted to mobile mid-warmup keeps its pre-demotion GPU flag but its eager-set cap drops. verified: getQuality at mobilePerf.ts:209, isMobileGPU at mobilePerf.ts:83.
- SINGLE KIT GLB vs FOUR FILES: ship ONE balustrade_kit.glb containing all named meshes/LODs (HYBRID/PERF approach) rather than four files (PHOTOREAL approach). Pays the DRACO decode cost once, one fetch, one cache entry, one atlas bind. Target <=280KB DRACO total.
- DRAW-CALL DISCIPLINE (binding): W3 must be net-zero/negative on mobile. Suppress the procedural baluX/baluZ/urn contributions to the merge lists when W3 is live via a scene.userData.w3_balustrade_active sentinel that the W2 lambdas check and early-return on (Z-fight + double-placement guard from the PERF brief). Desktop: 3 InstancedMesh (baluster, coping, finial) + ~6 urn clones. Mobile: 1 baluster IM (front terraces only) + 2 stair-foot urn clones. Potato: 0 GLBs and balustrades removed entirely (they read as noise at DPR 0.75).
- COLORSPACE/UV GATES: aoMap.channel=0 is hardcoded (verified assetLoader.ts:554) and diff uses SRGBColorSpace (verified assetLoader.ts:544) — author exactly ONE UV set (assert len(uv_layers)==1 in bpy before export) so GLTFLoader can't import AO on channel 1; let loadPBRSet own colorspace so no per-map fiddling in the loader wrapper.
- MATERIAL GATE: GLTFLoader bypasses mkPhys (verified mobilePerf.ts:339). After loadModel resolves, traverse every mesh and re-apply mkPhys with the shared travertine props + shared aoMap/normalMap/map, stripping any authored clearcoat/sheen. Author standard PBR only.
- FLAG GATE + RETIREMENT: const W3 = W2 && flag3d('w3_exterior') read once at top of the scene useEffect (verified flags3d.ts:41 semantics: default-on except prod hosts, ?flag3d override, sessionStorage-persisted). Document in flags3d.ts that W3 must NOT be retired until W2 is prod-promoted AND iOS WKWebView QA passes.
- MODEL-LOADER NOTE: loadModel already sets castShadow/receiveShadow on every mesh and returns a clone (verified modelLoader.ts:17-45); clones are safe to feed as InstancedMesh source geometry. Dispose IM geometry/material at cleanup but NEVER clearModelCache in cleanup (unmount only).

**Integration:**
- Single async seam inside the ExteriorScene.tsx scene useEffect, after the synchronous BufferGeometry pass, gated by the synchronous const W3 = W2 && flag3d('w3_exterior') (added at line 98).
- loadBalustradeSystem() calls preloadDraco() (new one-line export in modelLoader.ts) then loadModel('/models/exterior/balustrade_kit.glb') via the production-proven GLTFLoader+DRACOLoader path (decoder at /draco/, warm from bust GLBs).
- Extract lo/hi meshes by name; choose LOD by getQuality().maxEagerTextureSets (governor-safe: a demoted desktop keeps its stale isMobileGPU flag but its eager-set cap drops, so key off maxEagerTextureSets NOT isMobileGPU).
- Build ONE fresh MeshStandardMaterial via mkPhys FROM loadTravertineOrnamentTextures() (loaded once); assign by reference to every InstancedMesh — same THREE.Texture instances across all four meshes (the #1 iOS jetsam guard).
- Suppress the procedural baluX/baluZ/parapet/urn producers on the synchronous W3 boolean so the GLB path REPLACES rather than adds geometry (draw-call + Z-fight guard). scene.userData.w3_balustrade_active is a post-hoc assertion only.
- Register travertine_ornament in allTexSets so unmount disposes it exactly once via disposePBRSet and the traverse guard (buildCachedTextureSet skip-set) skips the shared maps.
- Everything in try/catch: on any reject the procedural path stays live (zero regression). Cleanup: existing blanket traverse disposes IM geometry/material; NEVER clearModelCache in cleanup (unmount-only, and it is interior-shared).

**LOD tiers:**
- DESKTOP (getQuality().maxEagerTextureSets===20): hi meshes (baluster_hi/urn_hi/finial_hi/coping), full instance set — baluster IM (all terraces+parapets) + coping IM + finial IM + ~6 urn clones
- MOBILE (maxEagerTextureSets===4, i.e. >2 && <=4): lo meshes, front-terrace baluster IM + 2 stair-foot urn clones only
- POTATO (maxEagerTextureSets<=2 OR shadowsEnabled===false): skip loadBalustradeSystem ENTIRELY — 0 GLBs, procedural balustrades also removed (they read as DPR-0.75 noise). Do NOT rely on a single <=4 threshold; branch 3-way explicitly.
- LODs authored as separately-named meshes inside ONE kit GLB: baluster_lo, baluster_hi, urn_lo, urn_hi, finial_lo, finial_hi, coping

**Dependencies:** modelLoader.ts must gain a `preloadDraco()` export (DRACOLoader is module-private; no warmup hook exists today) — or drop the warmup guard and accept cold-decoder latency., assetLoader.ts needs the thin loadTravertineOrnamentTextures wrapper (generic loadPBRSet(basePath,prefix,{repeat}) already covers it; aoMap.channel=0 forced at line 554)., Depends on W2 (flag3d('w2_exterior')) being live: W3 = W2 && flag3d('w3_exterior'). W3 must NOT be retired until W2 is prod-promoted AND iOS WKWebView QA passes (document in flags3d.ts)., Placement-array refactor: baluX/baluZ (607/615) inner loops must expose their per-baluster positions as a shared literal consumed by both the procedural merge and the InstancedMesh matrices (single source of truth for positions)., Shares the travertine_ornament PBR set with any future WS (dome ribs, capitals, coping-course) — author once, reuse by reference; keep total unique exterior PBR sets <=3-4 (mobile eager cap = 4)., toktx binary for the KTX2 fast-follow (optional; JPG ships first).

**Feasibility:**
- Perf risk: low
- iOS risk: medium
- Blender MCP can produce: yes
- Blocker: Async sentinel ordering (fix #6): using scene.userData.w3_balustrade_active to suppress procedural producers cannot work — procedural geometry is built and merged synchronously before the async GLB load resolves. Must suppress on the synchronous W3 boolean instead. Correctness blocker; ship-stopping if unfixed (double balusters + Z-fight at every waypoint).
- Blocker: mkPhys misuse (fix #1): the material-rewire step as specified is not implementable (mkPhys constructs, not patches). Must rewrite the loader to build a fresh material from the PBR set. Without this the GLBs render with GLTFLoader default materials (wrong palette, possible clearcoat on desktop, no baked AO wiring), defeating the whole fidelity goal.
- Blocker: Missed procedural baluster sources (fix #5): parapet-ring balusters at line 2729 and tower balustrade at 2200-2209 are not in the plan's suppression list; leaving them live means W3 is additive (not net-zero) on draw calls AND produces overlapping geometry.
- Fix: mkPhys IS A CONSTRUCTOR, NOT A PATCHER (verified mobilePerf.ts:339-367): it does `new MeshStandardMaterial(props)` from a props object; it does NOT accept or mutate an existing material. The plan's repeated instruction to 'traverse every mesh and re-apply mkPhys to strip clearcoat' is not implementable as written. FIX: after loadModel resolves, DISCARD the GLTFLoader-imported materials entirely and construct ONE fresh material via mkPhys(THREE,{color,roughness,map,normalMap,aoMap,...}) from the shared travertine_ornament set, then assign it to every InstancedMesh. Do not try to 'strip' authored clearcoat off a live GLTF material — just don't use that material at all. (This also means author-side clearcoat/sheen is irrelevant: it never reaches the runtime, so drop that authoring worry.)
- Fix: dracoLoader.preload() GUARD IS UNAVAILABLE (verified modelLoader.ts:1-45): the DRACOLoader instance is module-private and NOT exported; loadModel exposes no preload/warmup hook. The 'decoder-warmup race fix' via dracoLoader.preload() cannot be called from balustradeLoader.ts. FIX EITHER: (a) export `preloadDraco()` from modelLoader.ts that calls the private dracoLoader.preload(); OR (b) drop the guard — the bust GLBs already prove the decoder loads on demand and the seam is async/try-caught, so a cold decoder just adds latency, not failure. Recommend (a), one-line export, since W3 may run before any bust GLB in the exterior scene (busts are interior).
- Fix: aoMap.channel=0 IS OWNED BY loadPBRSet, NOT BY GLTFLoader (verified assetLoader.ts:554). A GLB's own embedded aoMap would import on whatever TEXCOORD the glTF declares (channel 1 if a 2nd UV exists). Since the plan (correctly) supplies AO from the shared travertine_ornament loadPBRSet — where channel=0 is forced — the GLB must NOT embed its own AO/textures at all. FIX: export the balustrade_kit.glb with NO embedded textures (geometry + UV0 only); assert exactly one UV layer in bpy before export (len(uv_layers)==1). The 'WEBP textures embedded' line from the routing doctrine CONTRADICTS this for W3 — for the balustrade kit, ship geometry-only GLB and drive all maps from the JS PBR set.
- Fix: UNMOUNT CLEANUP IS A BLANKET scene.traverse (verified ExteriorScene.tsx:4909-4922) that disposes EVERY geometry + material + non-cached texture. Consequence: (a) InstancedMesh geometry/material get disposed automatically — the plan's separate 'dispose IM into extraDisposables' is redundant but harmless; (b) the shared travertine_ornament textures WILL be disposed unless registered. If you register them in allTexSets (line 4923 disposePBRSet) that is correct for single-scene unmount. But the InstancedMesh material carries map/normalMap/aoMap by REFERENCE to the shared set — the traverse at 4915-4918 will call .dispose() on them once (guarded by _cachedSet). FIX: add the travertine_ornament set to buildCachedTextureSet()/allTexSets registry so it is disposed exactly once via disposePBRSet and skipped by the traverse guard — otherwise double-dispose warnings / GL errors. Verify buildCachedTextureSet includes it.
- Fix: LINE NUMBERS IN THE PLAN ARE STALE — RE-VERIFIED ACTUALS: baluX=ExteriorScene.tsx:607, baluZ=615 (both push CylinderGeometry(0.17,0.21,1.1,8) into gTrimR merge array — plan's dims are correct). Inline rooftop urn closure=2720 (pushes into gTrimM). Tower-cornice corner urns=2258-2263. Stair-foot bronze urns=~1360-1372 ('10 meshes'). Parapet-ring balusters (a SECOND baluster source the plan MISSED)=2729 (CylinderGeometry(0.14,0.18,1.0,6) inline). FIX: the sentinel-suppression must ALSO guard line 2729 and the tower balustrade at 2200-2209, or W3 leaves procedural balusters co-existing with GLB ones (double-placement + Z-fight, the exact bug the plan tries to prevent). Re-audit ALL baluster/urn producers, not the 4 the plan lists.
- Fix: SENTINEL-SUPPRESSION HAS AN ASYNC ORDERING HAZARD. The procedural baluX/baluZ/urn closures run SYNCHRONOUSLY in the geometry pass and are immediately mergeGeometries'd into a single static mesh (lines 646, 565). By the time the ASYNC loadBalustradeSystem resolves and sets scene.userData.w3_balustrade_active=true, the procedural balusters are ALREADY built and merged. An early-return checking the sentinel AT CLOSURE-CALL-TIME works ONLY if the flag is knowable synchronously. FIX: gate on the SYNCHRONOUS W3 boolean (const W3 = W2 && flag3d('w3_exterior'), read at top of useEffect) inside the closures — NOT on the async-set userData sentinel. The sentinel is useless for suppression because it is set too late. Use W3 for suppression; keep the sentinel only as a defensive post-hoc assertion. This is a correctness blocker.
- Fix: POTATO TIER IS UNGATED BY THE CHOSEN LOD KEY. Plan picks lo/hi by getQuality().maxEagerTextureSets<=4 => mobile geometry (verified thresholds: desktop=20, mobile=4, potato=2). That maps BOTH mobile(4) and potato(2) to the 'lo' mesh, but the plan also says 'potato = 0 GLBs, balustrades removed entirely'. maxEagerTextureSets<=4 is TRUE for potato too, so potato would load the kit unless separately gated. FIX: branch explicitly on tier: if potato (maxEagerTextureSets<=2 OR shadowsEnabled===false) => skip loadBalustradeSystem entirely (0 GLBs); elif <=4 => lo mesh + reduced instance count; else => hi mesh. Do not rely on a single <=4 threshold for a 3-way tier decision.
