### WS25 — Asset provenance & licensing

*Track CC0 vs Sketchfab-license vs Rodin/Hunyuan commercial terms for a PAID app; a license ledger + attribution plan.*

**Summary:** W3 exterior GLB pipeline: scripted-BPY hero assets (dome, capitals, balusters, drum-bay, fountain, tympanum, lantern, cornice, stair, herm) baked and DRACO-exported into public/models/exterior, gated behind flag3d('w3_exterior'), REPLACING procedural placeholders via refactored per-element handles, with a WS25 license+budget build gate. Requires four upfront fixes the feasibility audit flagged as false premises before any asset ships.
**Priority `P1` · ~18d · Feasible: yes · Confidence 0.62**

**Vision.** Raise the perceived quality of the exterior villa ~1000x by grafting a small set of Blender-authored, DRACO-compressed GLBs onto the existing procedural W2 scene — REPLACING (never adding to) the smooth-hemisphere dome, box-sticker drum windows, box-top capitals, cylinder balusters, and stacked-cylinder fountain that read as placeholders at the dolly beats. The synthesis resolves the three competing briefs (photoreal / perf-first / hybrid) in favor of HYBRID with a PERF-FIRST hard master: scripted BPY is the zero-risk backbone for ~90% of hero geometry (dome, capitals, balusters, cornices, drum bay, fountain tazza, tympanum, stair, tower massing), Polyhaven CC0 is the ONLY texture/HDRI scan source, and generative AI (Hunyuan3D primary / Rodin alternate) is quarantined to organic statuary behind a BLOCKING owner-signoff gate — until confirmed, BPY herm placeholders ship. Everything is gated behind a fresh flag3d('w3_exterior') (W3 = W2 && flag), and every asset carries a machine-readable ledger entry that fails the build if commercialOk !== true. The mobile/iOS WKWebView envelope (≤60k tris mobile LOD, ≤15 GLB draw calls, DRACO mandatory, ≤500KB/asset, ≤8–10MB hero payload, 4-material eager cap) is the binding constraint that overrides fidelity: any asset that cannot make its mobile LOD is desktop-only and quality-gated, not shipped to mobile. The single highest-ROI target is the 8-panel segmented ogival dome (visible at every waypoint); the single most-read frame is the WP3/7.5s tympanum name-beat (d=118), which drives dome+drum-windows+entrance-capitals to top priority. Reduced-motion stills at WP1/WP3/WP5 mean every hero asset must be correct at exactly those three front-dead-on angles.

**Design decisions:**
- HYBRID over PHOTOREAL-MAX and PERF-FIRST as the top-level lens, but with PERF-FIRST as the binding master: fidelity is pushed only within the iOS/WKWebView envelope (750k scene tris / 80 calls / 140MB tex QA gate; per-exterior-GLB budget ≤60k mobile LOD, ≤15 GLB draw calls, ≤500KB/asset). Any asset that busts mobile is tagged budgetTier='desktop' and gated on getQuality()/GPU tier — never shipped to mobile. This resolves the core tension: the CC-BY statue that pushes mobile over budget is rejected on PERF grounds regardless of license.
- GLBs must REPLACE procedural geometry on mobile/potato, never stack on top. In the W3 async load block, after each GLB resolves, hide/dispose the matching procedural equivalent (dome hemisphere, baluster cylinder rows, drum-window boxes, capital box-tops, fountain cylinders) wrapped in try/finally so the procedural stays visible on GLB reject. This is non-negotiable: the adaptive governor demotes a device one tier for 7 days if >20% of frames miss 25ms in the first 15s, so additive GLBs would spike draw calls during warmup and trigger demotion.
- Integration is additive-only against a solved seam: loadModel(path) in modelLoader.ts (GLTFLoader+DRACOLoader, decoder warm at /draco/ from the two bust GLBs which serve as the decoder canary) returns a cached clone. Load ASYNC inside the existing scene useEffect AFTER the synchronous procedural pass, each in its own try/catch → silent procedural fallback. Never open a 2nd WebGL context (use rendererPool.ts). Dispose only via clearModelCache() at unmount; never dispose clones. Re-apply mkPhys() to every loaded material because GLTFLoader bypasses it, and standard PBR only (BaseColor/Metallic/Roughness/Normal) — clearcoat/sheen/transmission are stripped on mobile.
- Fresh flag: flag3d('w3_exterior'), read ONCE at mount (never per-frame), W3 = W2 && flag3d('w3_exterior'). Staging-ON / prod-OFF is automatic via the PROD_HOSTS hostname check in flags3d.ts (verified). No W2 flag retirement until W3 is prod+iOS verified. ?flag3d=w3_exterior override works for on-device QA.
- WS25 license ledger is the single source of truth and a HARD build gate. One committed JSON file (docs/ASSET_LICENSE_LEDGER.json — NOT under public/, NOT gitignored) + scripts/check-asset-licenses.mjs run as a package.json prebuild hook AND in the Vercel build command before next build. Fails CI (exit 1, human-readable table) if: any entry touching public/models/exterior/** or public/textures/pbr/** has commercialOk !== true; any aiModel entry lacks aiTier or aiTier==='unconfirmed'/'free'; any source==='sketchfab' entry lacks explicit owner override + verified CC0/CC-BY license field. This means a license debt or NC/ND term physically cannot reach the Vercel bundle.
- Ledger ALSO carries perf metadata (triCount, budgetTier, textureSets) so the same gate enforces budgets: sum(triCount where budgetTier IN [mobile,all]) ≤ 60000; unique textureSets where budgetTier != desktop ≤ 4 (mobilePerf eager cap). One file carries both legal and perf truth — grafted from the perf-first brief onto the ledger-centric briefs.
- Generative AI is BLOCKED by default behind owner signoff. Hunyuan3D is PRIMARY (open-weights, Apache-2.0 weights/MIT code, outputs are owner IP, cheaper/less-gated, strong single-image organic reconstruction) for mascarons/herms/statuary; Rodin/Hyper3D is ALTERNATE for hero center-frame figures only (native GLB, cleaner topology, multi-image) — but Rodin FREE tier is non-commercial, so aiTier must be Pro+ and recorded. Until owner ticks the Blender N-panel checkbox, confirms tier, and a licenseProof screenshot is committed to docs/licenses/, the gate blocks these assets and BPY herm placeholders (capped column + rough-carved normal-mapped face, ~800 tris, sandstone PBR) ship instead. execute_blender_code probes bpy.context.scene.get('rodin_api_key','UNSET') to detect enablement.
- Sketchfab: SKIP entirely for W3. Disabled in N-panel + per-model NC/ND risk for a paid app. The gate treats source==='sketchfab' as a blocking error absent explicit owner override with a verified CC0/CC-BY license field read from get_sketchfab_model_preview. Scripted BPY + Hunyuan3D cover all needs with zero ambiguity.
- Textures: ≤3 shared atlased PBR sets to respect the 4-material mobile eager cap — 'stone' (travertine+plaster share UV tiles, Polyhaven-seeded normals but albedo repainted to canon PLASTER #F2E9DA / TRAVERTINE #E8DCC0), 'terracotta/coppo' (Polyhaven ceramic_roof_01 normal seed, albedo repainted to coppo #B0725A), 'metal-gold' (fully procedural noise+voronoi, no third-party source, GOLD #B8973A, metalness 0.85 / roughness 0.25). This keeps ledger Polyhaven provenance to ≤2 texture-set entries — trivially auditable.
- Instance repeats, merge uniques. Author ONE master GLB per repeated element (baluster, drum-window bay, urn, herm, cypress, buxus) and place via InstancedMesh with per-instance matrix + scale/rot jitter for the 'grown-over-centuries' asymmetry — never export 9 towers. Merge uniques (dome, fountain, tympanum, stair) per-material in Blender before export via mergeGeometries. Draw calls (not tri count) are the #1 mobile killer.
- Bake/lighting must MATCH the runtime one-sun/one-grade or the GLB clashes: Blender sun lamp = DirectionalLight #FFB870 at [-20,18,-30] (SW ~28° elevation, azimuth ~213°); bake AO into GLB ao channel on UV0 ONLY (aoMap.channel=0 is hardcoded; SSAO is desktop-only so baked AO carries mobile/potato); bake at exposure 1.0 (runtime NeutralToneMapping exposure 1.15 applied once — never per-asset); normal maps OpenGL convention (Blender default); emissive 1.5–3.0 to cross the 0.85 bloom threshold (lantern + tympanum gold ONLY); non-photo assets stay ≤0.6 relative luminance so memories remain the brightest pixels.
- Export contract: DRACO GLB (level 6, pos 14, nrm 10, uv 12, export_apply=True, export_yup=True, WEBP textures embedded) to public/models/exterior/<name>.glb. NEVER meshopt (no MeshoptDecoder registered — silent iOS fail). Assert GLB header at export (magic 0x46546C67, v2, extensionsUsed ⊇ KHR_draco_mesh_compression) and assert no KHR_mesh_quantization-without-draco. Strip Polyhaven EXTRAS metadata from objects before export. KTX2 is a fast-follow (npm run build:ktx2 needs toktx) via manifest feature-detect with per-file JPG/WEBP fallback — ship JPG/WEBP first, compress after.
- Every scripted BPY asset's Python source is committed to scripts/blender/exterior/*.py alongside its GLB, making provenance self-evident from git blame and re-export a single script run (critical for the tympanum, which embeds the owner's name as geometry and must be re-exported if the owner changes — with a documented fallback of keeping the name as the existing W2 Three.js TextGeometry overlay and shipping only the tympanum FRAME/depth GLB).
- LOD strategy per hero asset for the 18s dolly: desktop hi / mobile / potato. Dome ships all tiers (mobile ~2k, potato ~800 ultra-low, NO shadows/env on potato). Decorative GLBs (fountain tazza, urns) capped at 2 on mobile, 0 on potato. Distance-LOD swaps low geometry on wide dolly frames. **Integration:**
- Read flag once at mount: const W3 = W2 && flag3d('w3_exterior'); (W2 is already W1 && flag3d('w2_exterior') at ExteriorScene line 98). Never read per-frame.
- Add a W3 async block inside the existing scene useEffect AFTER the synchronous procedural W2 geometry pass. Prefetch: call dracoLoader.preload() + fetch dome.glb before/at cinematic start (FIX-1).
- Per hero GLB: try { const g = await loadExteriorModel('/models/exterior/dome.glb'); g.traverse(m => { if (m.isMesh) m.material = mkPhysFromGltf(m.material); applyShadowFlags(m); }); scene.add(g); hideProcedural(exteriorRefs.domeShell); } catch { /* procedural stays visible */ }. Wrap hide-procedural in try/finally so the procedural equivalent survives a GLB reject.
- Choose LOD path by getQuality()/isMobileGPU()/getGPUTier(): dome+lantern all tiers (potato ultra-low, no shadow/env, skip fetch if getGPUTier()==='potato'); decorative fountain/urn only when tier allows (<=2 mobile, 0 potato); statuary = herm on mobile, desktop-biased hero only if generative unblocked.
- Use InstancedMesh for baluster/drum_window/capital/herm/urn masters (per-instance matrix + scale/rot jitter for 'grown-over-centuries' asymmetry); uniques (dome, fountain, tympanum, lantern, stair) are merged-in-Blender single meshes.
- Use ONLY the pooled renderer (rendererPool.ts) — never open a 2nd WebGL context (iOS jetsam kills it silently). Dispose ONLY via clearModelCache() at unmount; never dispose clones.
- modelLoader edit (FIX-2): castShadow/receiveShadow conditional on getQuality().shadowsEnabled; convert GLTF materials via mkPhys semantics on every clone (GLTFLoader bypasses mkPhys; mkPhys(three,props) builds a fresh material, so translate GLTF props then strip Physical-only on mobile).
- CreditsPanel.tsx reads the ledger (static JSON import), renders only attributionRequired===true entries (expected 0 today: all Polyhaven CC0 + all BPY PROPRIETARY). Gated flag3d('w3_exterior') on staging; UN-gate on prod-promote.

**LOD tiers:**
- Desktop (hi): full decorative set, dome ~8k, real HDRI IBL (belfast_sunset_puresky_1k), SSAO on top of baked AO, shadows on.
- Mid-mobile (single authored LOD, <=750k scene / 60k exterior-GLB sum): dome ~2k, <=2 decorative GLBs, procedural PMREM env (no real-HDRI IBL), baked AO carries (SSAO is desktop-only), shadows per getQuality().shadowsEnabled.
- Potato: 0 decorative GLBs; dome only at <=800 ultra-low LOD, NO shadows, NO env map; dome GLB fetch skipped entirely when getGPUTier()==='potato' to avoid wasted texture download on a demoted device.
- Distance-LOD: swap dome_lo / capital_lo on wide dolly frames (WP1/WP2 far); dome_hi only when camera d<130 (WP3 name-beat and closer).

- Perf risk: high
- iOS risk: high
- Blender MCP can produce: yes
- Blocker: FALSE PREMISE: 'DRACO decoder already warm from bust GLBs / busts are the exterior canary.' Busts load only via bustBuilder.ts in the interior bust-builder panel; ExteriorScene.tsx has ZERO loadModel calls today. The exterior's first GLB triggers a COLD DRACO decoder init (~250KB wasm/js) mid-dolly inside the 15s governor warmup window, risking the >20%/25ms demotion the plan itself warns about.
- Blocker: FALSE PREMISE: 'additive-only, zero loader changes.' modelLoader.loadModel (lines 30-33) hardcodes castShadow=true/receiveShadow=true on every mesh and does NOT apply mkPhys. Plan requires potato=no-shadows and mkPhys re-application on every loaded material. Both require editing modelLoader (or post-processing every clone), so it is NOT zero-loader-change.
- Blocker: UNPROVEN RE-ARCHITECTURE (highest integration risk): the 'GLBs REPLACE procedural, hide/dispose the matching procedural equivalent (hideProcedural(domeHemisphere))' step assumes per-element handles exist. ExteriorScene merges to ~18 static draw calls via mergeGeometries (12x usage confirmed). If the dome hemisphere/baluster rows/drum boxes are baked into merged masonry draw calls, you cannot hide just one element without re-splitting the W2 merge. No evidence the merge exposes hideable per-element handles.
- Blocker: UNVALIDATED LONG POLE: the Blender bake+export pipeline is unproven end-to-end. MCP runs bpy and Polyhaven is enabled, but no Cycles GPU (HIP) bake + DRACO export + header-assert has been demonstrated through the MCP socket. ### WS26 — Cinematic dolly choreography w/ new hero

*Re-tune the 18s establishing dolly + reveal beats to showcase the dome/stair/statuary; reduced-motion variant.*

**Summary:** W3 exterior fidelity pass: 5 scripted-BPY hero GLBs (ogival dome, arched drum-window, Corinthian capital, lathe baluster, fluted tazza) authored in Blender 5.2, DRACO-compressed, streamed via existing modelLoader behind flag3d('w3_exterior'), replacing procedural primitives net-zero draw calls; all figural/statuary deferred until Rodin/Hunyuan are enabled.
**Priority `P1` · ~9d · Feasible: yes · Confidence 0.72**

**Vision.** Re-choreograph the existing 18s Catmull-Rom establishing dolly so that each beat lands on a hero Blender GLB at its maximum authored screen-real-estate, while the dome silhouette remains the unbroken protagonist and the ~7.5s tympanum-name frame becomes the single unmistakable money shot. This is a CHOREOGRAPHY-ONLY workstream: it authors NO Blender geometry itself, but owns (a) the drop-in GLB contract five upstream Blender workstreams must hit, (b) all camera/DOF/god-ray/vignette/lookAt retune code, and (c) the async load barrier that guarantees hero geometry is present before the dolly fires. The governing lens is HYBRID with a PERF-FIRST master: desktop gets the full photoreal cinematic pass (DOF rack-focus, additive god-ray quad, emissive-gold bloom, vignette pulse); mid-mobile/iOS is the binding budget and receives NONE of the postprocessing extras — it gets the identical GLB geometry (dome + drum-window only) plus the refined 3-still reduced-motion set. Every new line lives inside `const W3 = W2 && flag3d('w3_exterior')`; when W3 is off the render path is byte-identical to today's W2. Critically, the retune does NOT touch the 5 approved W2 waypoint coordinates (owner-signed 2026-08-06) — W3 only adds a lookAt override, per-beat DOF/vignette mutation, and the GLB barrier. The 1000x perceived-quality jump comes from swapping box-primitive dome/drum/capitals/balusters/fountain for carved GLBs exactly where the camera dwells, NOT from moving the camera.

**Design decisions:**
- LENS RESOLUTION — HYBRID geometry, PERF-FIRST budget, PHOTOREAL desktop-only postprocessing. The photoreal brief's DOF/god-ray/vignette stack is adopted but hard-gated to `!isMobileGPU()` desktop; mobile/iOS gets identical GLB geometry with ZERO new postprocessing. This resolves the core tradeoff: mobile pays only the geometry cost (which REPLACES procedural, net-zero draw calls), desktop pays the cinematic cost it can afford.
- WAYPOINTS ARE FROZEN. All three briefs agreed the 5 W2 waypoint [theta,phi,d] values are owner-approved (2026-08-06) and must not move. W3 adds only: (1) a lookAt override, (2) per-beat DOF/vignette uniform mutation, (3) the GLB barrier. The W2 waypoint array is never edited — verified the code reads a static W2 path.
- LOOKAT — adopt the perf-first brief's CONDITIONAL raise, NOT the photoreal brief's global raise. Verified anchors: HILL_Y=8, drumBaseY=vH+5.5, rDrumH=11.0, rDomeR=8.0, so dome origin = drumBaseY+rDrumH+0.2 and apex ~ origin+8. Photoreal brief's lookAt(0,23,0) risks pushing the door into the lower third at r=35. RESOLUTION: under W3, lerp lookAt.y from HILL_Y+14 (=22, wide/tympanum beats, keeps lantern crown in top 20%) back down to HILL_Y+10 (=18) across beat 5 (r=63->35) so the entrance door re-centres for the EntranceHall handoff. Never a global raise.
- GLB BARRIER — adopt the photoreal Promise.all barrier BUT with the perf-first brief's timeout + graceful-veil fallback. Fire cinematicResumed only after Promise.allSettled([...glbLoads]) resolves OR a 4s timeout elapses (whichever first). On timeout, fire the dolly anyway; try/catch procedural fallback covers any late-arriving GLB with an invisible mid-dolly swap. Reduced-motion path uses a 0.15-opacity holding veil until GLBs settle, then crossfades — so stills never freeze on procedural geometry on a fast connection.
- GPU-UPLOAD SCHEDULING — adopt the perf-first brief's requestIdleCallback deferral to dodge the adaptive governor. loadModel() resolves a cached clone but adds nothing to the scene synchronously (verified modelLoader.ts lines 27-37). W3 must schedule scene.add() + mkPhys() traversal via requestIdleCallback (200ms timeout fallback) so the one-frame BufferGeometry GPU upload never lands inside the 0-15s governor measurement window's first rendered frame. This prevents a 7-day potato demotion.
- mkPhys() RE-APPLICATION IS MANDATORY. Verified loadModel() does NOT call mkPhys(). Every loaded GLB material must be traversed and re-wrapped: child.material = mkPhys(child.material). Missing this renders the dome at full metalness on mobile. Confirm mkPhys preserves emissiveIntensity (it sets roughness/metalness/envMapIntensity only) before relying on the gold pulse.
- DRAW-CALL NET-ZERO. Each GLB REPLACES its procedural counterpart, removed from centralGroup on resolve — never additive. Desktop net delta 0; iOS loads only dome+drum-window and removes the procedural dome hemisphere + the existing 12 BoxGeometry drum windows (verified at lines 1786-1788), net delta 0. Dev overlay asserts renderer.info.render.calls stays flat.
- POTATO TIER — 0 decorative GLBs, dome LOD only. potato loads dome_ogival_lod.glb (<=2.5k tris) or keeps the procedural SphereGeometry hemisphere if even the LOD 404s; skips drum-window/capital/baluster/tazza entirely. No DOF, no god-ray, no vignette, no env map.
- GOLD BLOOM — the lantern finial and tympanum name must exceed the 0.85 bloom luminanceThreshold at exposure 1.15. Set the lantern M.goldBright emissiveIntensity >= 1.8 (GOLD raw luminance ~0.52 is below threshold). For the tympanum add a thin emissive backing plane (emissive GOLD #B8973A, intensity 0.4) behind the existing MeshBasic name canvas so it kisses the threshold in screen space at beat 2 only.
- REDUCED-MOTION STILLS keep the exact WP0/WP2/entrance [theta,phi,d] positions; upgrade only framing (one-frame DOF snap on desktop, bokehScale 1.5) and the async holding-veil. On desktop, SSAO+SMAA still run for genuine high-fidelity freeze-frames.
- DOF SHADER PRE-WARM — call setDOF() once at scene mount with beat-0 values so the DepthOfFieldEffect compiles up front; focusDistance/bokehScale are uniforms (not #defines) in the postprocessing lib, so per-beat mutation won't recompile. Guards against a first-rack stutter.
- RENDER-ORDER — set terrain renderOrder=1, sky sphere renderOrder=0, god-ray quad renderOrder=-1 (frustumCulled=false) to prevent Z-fight without extra depth writes. Desktop-only.

**Integration:**
- 1. flags3d.ts: NO change needed - flag3d('w3_exterior') works by naming convention (default ON except prod hosts). Declare const W3 = W2 && flag3d('w3_exterior') read ONCE at scene mount (after the skySphere block), never per frame.

Kick off all loadModel() calls immediately at scene-mount (DRACO decoder already warm from bust GLBs), gated by tier: desktop = all 5; iOS/isMobileGPU() = dome + drum_window only; potato = dome_ogival_lod only (or keep procedural). loadModel(path) returns a cached clone and adds NOTHING to the scene synchronously (verified modelLoader lines 27-37).
- 3. Per resolved load: DEFER scene.add() + material fix-up via requestIdleCallback (200ms fallback), scheduled to COMPLETE before ~2.4s (the governor warmup ends at GOV_WARMUP_MS=2500ms; the 0-15s dolly IS the sampled window - a late upload spike risks a 7-day potato demotion). Set the GLB invisible until fully added, then remove the replaced procedural mesh from centralGroup (net-zero calls). try/catch -> keep procedural on reject.
- 4. MATERIAL FIX-UP (corrected): mkPhys(three, props) CONSTRUCTS from a props object - it does NOT wrap an existing material, so 'child.material = mkPhys(child.material)' is WRONG. GLTFLoader emits MeshStandardMaterial by default (not Physical), so DO NOT strip clearcoat. Instead traverse each loaded material and ASSERT: aoMap && aoMap.channel=0, correct roughness/metalness, envMapIntensity set to match scene, and emissiveIntensity preserved for gold. Only rebuild via mkPhys(three, extractedProps) if a Physical-only field is present.
- 5. Promise.allSettled([...glbLoads]) with a 4s timeout; fire cinematicResumed on settle-OR-timeout (whichever first). Reduced-motion path shows a 0.15-opacity holding veil until GLBs settle then crossfades (stills never freeze on procedural on a fast link).
- 6. Postprocessing per-beat (desktop only, !isMobileGPU()): capture dofEffect+vignetteEffect refs from the refactored createPostProcessing return; pre-warm setDOF() once at mount (focusDistance/bokehScale are uniforms not #defines - no recompile on mutation); mutate per beat off the existing ot clock. Add god-ray PlaneGeometry(200,200) quad renderOrder=-1 frustumCulled=false (desktop only) and an emissive-GOLD backing plane behind the tympanum canvas (W3, intensity ~0.4).
- 7. lookAt (corrected against frozen code): live code is camera.lookAt(0, HILL_Y+(W2?13:8), 0) as a CONSTANT (line 4694) - W2 already sits at +13 (=21). W3 may ONLY override this one line to a conditional lerp (HILL_Y+14 wide/tympanum beats -> HILL_Y+10 across beat 5 for the EntranceHall handoff); do NOT edit the 5 frozen WP arrays (lines ~4618-4623) or the reduced-motion stills (lines ~4564-4568).
- 8. GOLD bloom: lantern goldBright emissiveIntensity >=1.8 (GOLD raw luminance is below the 0.85 threshold at exposure 1.15); tympanum backing plane emissive ~0.4. Reuse the pooled renderer (rendererPool) - NEVER open a 2nd WebGL context (iOS jetsam kills it silently). Dispose only via clearModelCache() at unmount; never dispose clones.
- 9. i18n: no new user-facing strings (tympanum name already localised via makeFrauncesLabel).

### WS27 — Signage & Fraunces wing signposts

*Integrate the existing Fraunces wing labels / owner-name tympanum with the new geometry (anchors, occlusion, legibility).*

**Summary:** WS27 "La Pietra Parla": Blender-script 4 carved-stone GLB substrates (tympanum panel + low-LOD, entrance stele, gold palmette acroterion, guttae metope) that float under the LIVE Fraunces canvas name at the WP3 dolly beat, gated W3=W2&&flag3d('w3_exterior'), reusing the existing travertine PBR set, +2 desktop/+1 mobile draw calls, with a corrected reskinLoadedMaterial() replacing the mkPhys misuse.
**Priority `P2` · ~4d · Feasible: yes · Confidence 0.78**

**Vision.** WS27 — "La Pietra Parla" (the stone speaks). Replace the exterior's two flat lettering surfaces — the CanvasTexture tympanum name and the box-stack entrance signpost — with Blender-authored carved-stone architecture, WITHOUT touching the Fraunces canvas lettering, the click/hover contracts, or i18n. The keystone insight, verified against ExteriorScene.tsx: the owner name must stay a LIVE canvas overlay (personal, i18n, font-aware, redraw-on-hydrate via tymNameRedrawRef); Blender contributes only the ARCHITECTURAL SUBSTRATE the canvas floats over — a bas-relief tympanum panel with a cartouche recess + egg-and-dart border, sculpted acroterion finials, a guttae-metope frieze fill, and a pietra-serena entrance stele. Every GLB is a drop-in Group at an existing seam anchor, gated W3 = W2 && flag3d('w3_exterior'), async-loaded after the synchronous geometry pass, try/catch → procedural fallback (the current shipped meshes stay in scene and are only hidden on GLB success). Net draw-call delta: +2 desktop, +1 mobile, 0 potato. This lifts the single most-read frame in the 18s dolly (WP3 tympanum beat, d=118) from "painted plane" to "chiselled stone" while keeping the personal name pixel-perfect.

**Design decisions:**
- NAME STAYS CANVAS, STONE BECOMES GLB (resolves the 3-brief split). Brief 1's per-user server-baked tympanum_{userId}.glb is REJECTED: it requires headless Blender-on-GPU server infra that does not exist, breaks i18n/live-hydrate, and re-bakes per name change. Brief 2 and Brief 3 both converge on keeping the canvas name overlay and making only the substrate a GLB — that is the winner. The GLB carries NO name text; the existing drawTymName canvas (tymNameRedrawRef) remains the authoritative personal surface at renderOrder 2, depthWrite:false.
- VERIFIED SEAM POINTS (from source, not brief estimates). tymMesh anchor = (0, pedBaseY+0.05, vestZ-1.13), pedBaseY=7.9, pedHalfSpan=6.2, pediment height 1.1. namePlane = PlaneGeometry(5.6,0.875) at (0, 8.28, vestZ-1.16), rotation.y=Math.PI, renderOrder 2. The GLB tympanum panel replaces tymMesh (set tymMesh.visible=false on GLB success) at the SAME anchor; its cartouche recess floor sits at vestZ-1.13, recessed 0.04 inward, so the canvas at vestZ-1.16 floats 0.03 proud of the recess floor — no coplanarity. Adopt Brief 3's polygonOffset(-2,-2) on the namePlane material as a belt-and-braces z-fight guard (ships in W2, no flag).
- GOLD CANON CORRECTION. Canon.ts GOLD = #D4AF37 (frames + tympanum only). The briefs' #B8973A / #B85C38 are the darker albedo-TARGETS from the perf brief and EMBER respectively — do NOT use #B8973A for the sun-grazed gold; author gold letters/finials at #D4AF37 albedo, roughness 0.25, metalness 0.9, NO emissive (spec-read only, per Brief 1). The tympanum SLAB is TRAVERTINE_GROUT #E3D6BC (matches the live W1 tymMat exactly), roughness 0.72, metalness 0.
- SIGNPOST: PRESERVE THE HIT-BOX SIBLING CONTRACT (missed by all three briefs). In source, addSignpost builds group g containing base+shaft+cap meshes AND makeFrauncesLabel AND a hit Mesh pushed to clickTargets with userData{roomId,accent:EMBER}. The GLB replaces ONLY the three procedural stone meshes; the Fraunces label (lbl at local 0,1.85,0.19) and the hit box (3.2×3.4×1.6) stay as-is siblings in g. This keeps the tap/hover contract and i18n label byte-identical. Choose Brief 3's tapered cippus (grown-centuries taper + chamfer + shallow acanthus cap + label recess) over Brief 1's octagonal-Attic cippus and Brief 2's mini-aedicula: the aedicula's two fluted columns cost ~340 tris for an element only seen at WP4/close-up, and its inscribed-field geometry conflicts with the existing sibling label placement. Simpler tapered stele = better ROI.
- MOBILE/POTATO TIERING. Mobile (isMobileGPU): load ONLY tympanum_panel_lo.glb (the WP3 hero); skip finials, metope, and stele GLB — procedural fallbacks stay. Potato: zero GLB loads. This honors the integration-seam brief's ≤15 GLB draw-call ceiling and keeps mobile GLB payload ≤200KB. Author one mobile LOD per hero asset (tympanum ≤1200 tris, no bevel/rustication) since the governor demotes presets not meshes — mobile geometry == potato geometry.
- ACROTERIA + METOPE ARE DESKTOP-ONLY POLISH (from Brief 1, budget-bounded). Replace the 3 ConeGeometry acroteria (M.bronze) with a gold palmette finial GLB instanced at the 3 existing positions (center pedApex, ±pedHalfSpan). Add a guttae-rosette metope GLB instanced 5× between the 6 existing triglyphs (line 1180-1183, at vestZ-1.05). Both desktop-only, both share the travertine_sign PBR set + M.gold, both merge-per-material so net desktop draw-call delta stays +2 total.
- BAKE ALIGNMENT IS NON-NEGOTIABLE. Blender sun = SUN lamp aimed along normalize([-20,18,-30]) = (-0.539,0.486,-0.690), color #FFB870, bake at exposure 1.0 (runtime applies 1.15 once via postprocessing). OpenGL normals (Blender default). Bake AO+curvature(Pointiness) into aoMap UV0 channel 0 (assetLoader forces aoMap.channel=0) so the carved-edge catch-light survives on the mobile procedural-PMREM env where gold specular flattens (Brief 1 mitigation).
- FLAG + FALLBACK DISCIPLINE. W3 = W2 && flag3d('w3_exterior') read once at mount. All loads via Promise.allSettled after the synchronous pass; on any reject, procedural counterpart stays visible (current shipped behavior = zero regression). Re-apply mkPhys() to every loaded MeshStandardMaterial (GLTFLoader bypasses the pipeline). Never dispose clones; clearModelCache() at unmount only. Two bust GLBs already warm the DRACO decoder before these load. No flag retirement until prod+iOS verified.

Verified src/lib/3d/mobilePerf.ts:339 — mkPhys(three, props) CONSTRUCTS a new material from a props object; it does NOT mutate an existing GLTF material. As written this is a no-op/crash. ### WS28 — Rollout: flags, A/B, perf gates, verification

*flag3d gating, staging->prod promotion, automated perf-regression gates, device checklist, deploy via npx vercel --prod.*

**Summary:** WS28 W3 exterior GLB rollout harness: a single w3AssetLoader.ts wrapper over the existing loadModel(), gated by flag3d('w3_exterior'), streaming scripted-BPY Blender GLBs (dome, capital, baluster, drum-window, urn, fountain-tazza) that hide-replace procedural W2 geometry per device tier, with cold-decoder warmup, own-position InstancedMesh, hybrid fallback, and a tris/draw-call perf overlay. No new Capacitor build.
**Priority `P1` · ~9d · Feasible: yes · Confidence 0.72**

**Vision.** WS28 is the rollout harness, not an authoring workstream: it safely promotes every Blender-authored W3 exterior GLB from flag-gated staging through automated perf-regression gates to prod+iOS, without breaking the adaptive governor, the iOS free-tier seal, or the 18s establishing dolly. It owns exactly four things and nothing else: (1) the flag3d('w3_exterior') gate wired so W3 = W2 && flag3d('w3_exterior'), read once at mount; (2) a single thin loader wrapper (w3AssetLoader.ts) over the existing loadModel() that normalises every GLB — mkPhys re-apply, aoMap.channel=0, per-clone material clone, multi-material merge — and counts draw calls; (3) tier-gated LOD asset selection + InstancedMesh placement so W3 GLBs REPLACE procedural geometry rather than add to it; and (4) a perf-assertion overlay + a binding device checklist whose gating device is iOS WKWebView in Capacitor. The governing lens is HYBRID: W2 procedural geometry always stays as the visible fallback, W3 GLBs load async on top and hide (never dispose) their procedural twin only on successful resolve, so potato tiers and any governor-demoted or GLB-failed device always see a correct W2 scene, never a broken half-W3 one. Perf ceilings are hard blocking floors on mobile/iOS and soft fidelity-first targets on desktop, resolving the photoreal-vs-perf tension per-tier rather than globally. No new Capacitor build is needed — GLBs load at runtime from the web bundle, so staging QA via ?flag3d=w3_exterior fully exercises the iOS path with the reviewer's existing TestFlight build.

**Design decisions:**
- FLAG WIRE (zero flags3d.ts changes): flag3d() is already generic and hostname-based (verified: PROD_HOSTS gate, ?flag3d override, sessionStorage persistence). In ExteriorScene.tsx, immediately after the W2 const declare `const W3 = W2 && flag3d('w3_exterior');`. Every W3 GLB load, InstancedMesh, and W3-specific PBR set sits inside `if (W3) { ... }`. Staging auto-ON, prod auto-OFF, ?flag3d=w3_exterior override and ?flag3d=-w3_exterior A/B toggle both work as-is (readOverrides handles the minus form).
- ONE INTEGRATION PRIMITIVE, NOT SCATTERED CODE: resolve the three briefs' divergent inline patterns by centralising into a single new file src/lib/3d/w3AssetLoader.ts — a thin wrapper over the EXISTING loadModel() from modelLoader.ts (never a new GLTFLoader/DRACOLoader — a 2nd loader risks a 2nd WebGL context = silent iOS jetsam). This keeps ExteriorScene.tsx's 4944-line useEffect changes minimal (one const + one async block) and puts all normalisation logic in one testable place.
- CLONE-MATERIAL SAFETY (critical, verified against modelLoader source): loadModel() caches the master and returns model.clone(); a THREE clone SHARES material references with the master. So before mkPhys-replacing a clone's material, w3AssetLoader MUST first `child.material = child.material.clone()` per mesh, then replace. Otherwise the first clone's mkPhys mutates the cached master and every subsequent clone/scene inherits it. This corrects the naive 'replace child.material' pattern in two of the three briefs.
- MKPHYS + AO CONTRACT ENFORCED IN THE WRAPPER: after each GLB resolves, traverse and for every Mesh: clone material, then `child.material = mkPhys(THREE, { color, map, normalMap, roughnessMap, aoMap, roughness, metalness })`, set `material.aoMapIntensity = 1.0`, `material.envMapIntensity = isMobileGPU() ? 0.3 : 0.8`, and force `if (material.aoMap) material.aoMap.channel = 0` (hardcoded in assetLoader.ts — a mismatch loses baked AO on mobile/potato where SSAO is off). GLTFLoader bypasses mkPhys; without this, MeshPhysicalMaterial clearcoat/sheen/transmission lands on iOS and spikes fragment cost 2-3x.
- DRAW-CALL IS THE #1 MOBILE KILLER, NOT TRI COUNT: every repeated element is InstancedMesh, never per-instance scene.add(). baluster_master → InstancedMesh(geo, mat, 80 desktop / 40 mobile / 0 potato). capital → InstancedMesh(×12/×6/0). drum window tile → InstancedMesh(×12). Instance matrices come from the Float32Array of column/baluster positions already computed in the W2 geometry pass. Uniques (dome shell, fountain) are single scene.add(). Multi-material GLBs (fountain basin+mascaron+water) are collapsed to <=2 draw calls via mergeGeometries (three/examples/jsm/utils/BufferGeometryUtils) per material-group BEFORE scene.add, inside the wrapper.
- HYBRID FALLBACK — HIDE THE TWIN, DON'T DISPOSE MID-LOOP: on successful GLB resolve, set the procedural counterpart `.visible = false` (disposing mid-render-loop causes a GPU stall and risks race with the raf). Never create the procedural mesh at all only when it is cheap to skip synchronously; otherwise build it (fallback) and hide on resolve. On GLB reject, leave procedural visible — the scene stays at correct W2 appearance. This is the single most important z-fight-avoidance rule (W2 already has ~25 documented z-fights; W3 must add zero).
- TIER-GATED LOD SELECTION drives which file loads, via getQuality()/isMobileGPU(): desktop = full set (dome_hi, capital, baluster, fountain_tazza, urn, drum_windows); mobile = dome_lo + fountain_tazza_lo ONLY (2 GLBs, <=60k tris, <=2 draw calls after merge/instance); potato = w3AssetLoader returns early, 0 decorative GLBs (optionally dome_potato <=10k flat-travertine if it exists, else pure procedural). LOD path is base name + suffix (_lo/_potato) constructed inside the wrapper — one code path, tier picks the suffix.
- GOVERNOR-SAFE LOAD TIMING (resolves the three briefs' conflicting mitigations): the governor samples the first 15s and demotes 7 days if >20% frames miss 25ms in 2 of 4 windows, with GOV_WARMUP_MS=2.5s. Do BOTH: (a) call dracoLoader.preload() (or a 50-tri canary load) as the very first thing in the W3 block to warm the WASM decoder during the free warmup window; (b) stagger scene.add()/InstancedMesh builds one-per-frame via a micro-scheduler (queueMicrotask/setTimeout(fn,0) between adds) so no single frame's GLTF-parse+scene.add exceeds ~8ms. Do NOT adopt the 'defer all adds to setTimeout(16000)' idea from one brief — it makes the hero dome pop in 16s into an 18s dolly, visibly wrong at the WP3 tympanum name-beat; staggered early load beats blanket deferral.
- PERF-ASSERTION OVERLAY (informs, does not block): a W3-gated DOM badge (visible when flag3d('w3_exterior') && NODE_ENV!=='production', or ?perfhud=1) reads renderer.info.render.triangles and renderer.info.render.calls once/sec for the first 20s. Green under ceiling, amber at 80%, red over. Ceilings by getQuality() tier — desktop <=200k tris / <=30 W3 GLB calls (scene <=180); mobile/iOS <=60k tris / <=15 W3 GLB calls (scene <=80). Also extend perfAssert.ts sample() with one W3-gated condition and PerfHud.tsx with 'tris' + 'W3 calls' rows (W3 calls from a window.__w3DrawCalls__ counter the wrapper increments on load, resets at unmount). Promotion is blocked manually if red fires on mobile tier.
- DISPOSE CONTRACT (verified against clearModelCache): do NOT call clearModelCache() at exterior unmount — the cache is shared with bust GLBs used by other scenes; clearing it disposes their masters. Instead track every W3 root Group in a w3Roots[] at the top of the useEffect and, in cleanup AFTER the existing scene.traverse dispose, per-clone dispose geometry+materials for each w3Root (clones own their cloned materials from the safety step; W3 clone geometry is shared with the cache master, so dispose geometry only if you did not also want cache reuse — prefer disposing only the cloned MATERIALS + InstancedMesh instances, leave clone geometry to clearModelCache's owner). Net: never double-dispose, never touch the shared cache.
- GOVERNOR TELEMETRY BEFORE FLAG RETIREMENT: in mobilePerf.ts governorDemote(), after the localStorage.setItem, add `try { window.posthog?.capture('mp3d_governor_demote', { from, to, renderer }); } catch {}`. Flag retirement is HARD-BLOCKED until this event rate is <1% of exterior sessions over a 48h prod soak AND a fresh on-device 18s-dolly-at-60fps recording is delivered to the owner.
- STAGING -> PROD PROMOTION CEREMONY: (a) drop pipeline_canary.glb (50-tri cube) first, verify magic bytes 0x46546C67 + v2 + extensionsUsed includes KHR_draco_mesh_compression, and that it loads + HUD shows W3 calls=1 + no leak on nav-away/back; (b) author real GLBs only after canary passes; (c) run full device checklist (see integration); (d) owner reviews W3 on staging at WP1/WP3/WP5 (reduced-motion stills) + WP2; (e) merge to committed master, `npx vercel --prod` (Git integration broken, CLI only per reference_vercel_deploy.md); (f) verify prod shows W2 by default and ?flag3d=w3_exterior on prod shows W3 (canary); (g) retire flag (delete the if(W3) guard, make unconditional) ONLY after the 48h soak gate above.

But InstancedMesh built FROM a clone's geometry shares that geometry with the cache master — disposing the InstancedMesh.geometry at unmount corrupts the cached master for the next mount. Fix: InstancedMesh must use geometry.clone() (or a freshly-merged geometry the wrapper owns), and the wrapper must return a manifest of exactly which geometries/materials it OWNS vs SHARES so cleanup disposes only owned resources. This is the single highest-risk correctness bug in the plan.

The 18s dolly starts immediately; async GLBs resolving mid-dolly means the hero dome/capitals POP IN during the cinematic on slow connections — visibly wrong exactly at the WP3 tympanum name-beat. The plan's 'staggered early load beats blanket 16s defer' is correct, but there is NO stated network-time budget or a 'hold dolly until hero dome resolved OR 3s timeout' fallback. Fix: gate the dolly start (or the WP3 beat) on Promise.race([domeLoaded, timeout(Nms)]) so you never dolly-reveal a half-loaded hero; and preload the dome GLB via the existing scenePreloader so it is in HTTP cache before the exterior mounts.

## Appendix D — Completeness Critics (gaps to still address)

1. **Interactive door/entrance affordance + EMBER hover state for the new hero geometry** — EMBER #B85C38 is reserved in canon for interactive-only surfaces, and the exterior has ~198 hover/raycast/door references, but NO workstream owns the entrance portal itself, the door leaves, or how the new GLB entrance columns/tympanum re-register raycasting and the EMBER hover glow. WS04 ships the stair/tympanum and WS27 the signage, but neither wires the interactive door affordance that lets a visitor actually ENTER the palace. If GLBs replace procedural entrance meshes, the click-to-enter hit target and its emissive hover feedback silently break — a functional regression, not just cosmetic.
2. **Atmospheric FX: chimney smoke, drifting clouds, birds, dust motes, volumetric god-rays** — The 18s golden-hour dolly's perceived quality depends heavily on air and life, not just masonry. WS19 covers code-only post-grade (bloom/DOF/vignette) and WS18 covers HDRI/AO, but nothing owns animated chimney smoke from the casa-torri, slow cloud drift, a few wheeling birds, floating dust/pollen motes in the sun shafts, or volumetric light. A pristine but STILL and LIFELESS villa reads as a render, not a place — this is a major 1000x-perception lever left entirely uncovered.
3. **Water simulation/animation upgrade (surface shader, flow, spray, caustics, reflections)** — WS12 explicitly keeps ALL water surfaces procedural and only swaps the fountain BODY geometry; WS11/WS13 defer water. So the actual water — the highest-drama element of a Renaissance villa (parterre pools, catena d'acqua, fountain jets/spray, ripples, screen-space reflections, caustics) — gets zero fidelity uplift. A carved travertine tazza filled with a flat blue disc undercuts the whole hero-fountain investment. No workstream owns animated water or reflection of the new dome in the pools.
4. **Ground-plane transition and contact grounding (AO decals, dirt buildup, moss/weathering at base joins)** — Every new GLB (dome base, tower feet, fountain plinth, balustrade, statuary pedestals, stair) meets the terrain, but no workstream owns the GROUND CONTACT — baked ground-shadow decals, dirt/moss accumulation at wall-to-earth joins, gravel scatter around plinths, or path-edge blending. Floating/pasted-on assets with a hard seam at the terrain are the #1 tell of cheap CG. WS15 does terrain/basamento but not the per-asset grounding contract that ties hero GLBs to the hill.
5. **Night/dusk state and artificial lighting of the villa (lit windows, glowing lantern at dusk, warm interior spill)** — daylightCycle.ts exists and the emissive gold lantern is authored, but no workstream defines the villa's appearance across the daylight cycle — lit window emissive at dusk, warm glow from the drum thermal-bays, lantern actually illuminating as a light source at night, or how baked AO/albedo holds up under non-golden-hour sun. All bakes are pinned to one sun at exposure 1.0; the plan never validates the assets at other times of day the runtime can render.
6. **Approach road, gates, and arrival sequence assets (the strada, entrance gate, boundary wall, drive)** — WS15 mentions a gravel strada and dry-stone wall as texture/tiling, but the ARRIVAL — the cypress-lined approach avenue terminating at a monumental gate between the two gate-towers, wrought-iron gates, boundary walls, gate piers with finials — is a signature Sette Sorelle motif and a natural dolly beat, yet no workstream owns the gate geometry or the framed approach composition. WS03 does gate-tower CROWNS only, not the gate structure itself.
7. **Distant landscape context: hill towns, cascine, campanili on the horizon, layered atmospheric depth** — The brief lists 'missing landscape cascine (2-3 stone farmhouses)' as a low-priority fidelity gap, but NO workstream picks it up (WS15 is terrain/walls/road only). The mid-and-far Tuscan context — distant hill-town silhouette, a far campanile, layered cypress ridgelines, aerial-perspective haze — is what sells scale and place behind the hero villa at wide waypoints. Currently the villa sits on empty hills with nothing beyond, capping the perceived-quality ceiling.
8. **Reduced-motion still composition + first-frame/LCP asset for the three hero angles** — The brief states reduced-motion composes stills at WP1/WP3/WP5 and 'every hero asset must be correct at exactly those three angles,' and multiple WS flag that GLBs must be awaited before stills compose or they pop in — but NO workstream OWNS the reduced-motion still pipeline, the await-all-heroes-before-compose gate, or the low-effort first-paint/poster image. This cross-cutting correctness requirement is scattered as a dependency across WS15/WS17/WS26 with no accountable owner, so it will fall through.
9. **i18n, accessibility, and settings surface for the W3 exterior (labels, alt-text, quality toggle, motion pref)** — Project rules mandate i18n + reduced-motion on every new component, but the 28 WS are entirely 3D-asset/perf focused and none owns the user-facing surface: translated names for new landmarks/tour stops, alt/aria descriptions of the exterior for screen readers, a settings toggle to force-disable W3 assets on a struggling device, or the 'why is my palace loading slowly' UX. Ships as an untranslated, inaccessible black-box.
10. **Seasonal/foliage color state and dead-vs-live vegetation coherence** — WS13 (buxus/garden) and WS14 (cypress/olive) author foliage against one golden-hour bake, but nothing owns seasonal coherence — wheat field green-vs-golden state, flowering vs dormant lavender/poppy, autumn tint, or how foliage albedo harmonizes with the villa palette across the daylight cycle. Mismatched vivid-green buxus against warm travertine under a dusk sun is a common immersion-breaker with no owner.
11. **Bust-builder and interior-portal asset regression guard under W3** — The only production GLBs today are bust_base/bust_female (the DRACO decoder canary) loaded by the interior bust-builder, and multiple WS warn clearModelCache() at exterior unmount would dispose the busts' shared masters. But no workstream owns REGRESSION-TESTING the bust builder and interior scene after W3 lands — the cache/dispose contract is treated per-WS, yet the failure mode (invisible busts, corrupted interior) is a cross-boundary bug that needs a dedicated verification owner.
12. **Coats-of-arms / heraldic cartouche and owner-personalization surfaces beyond the tympanum name** — The tympanum name-beat (WS04/WS19/WS25) is covered, but a Renaissance villa's identity also lives in a heraldic stemma/coat-of-arms cartouche over the portal, keystone masks, and family device — all figural relief flagged as generative-blocked. Owner personalization is a core product theme ('un corpo unico... bearing the owner's name'), yet the only personalization asset planned is flat lettering. No scripted fallback (e.g. a plain carved cartouche frame awaiting an uploaded crest) is owned by any WS.
13. **Renderer ownership is contradicted across workstreams: ExteriorScene owns a LOCAL `new THREE.WebGLRenderer()` (line 242-243), not the pool** — Verified: ExteriorScene.tsx:242-243 constructs its own renderer and appends `ren.domElement` at line 250; it never calls borrowRenderer(). Yet WS02/WS17/WS28 base their integration and their draw-call assertions on `getPooledRenderer().info` / `rendererPool`, and the doctrine repeatedly says 'use the pooled renderer, NEVER a 2nd context.' Only WS22 caught this. The plan hand-waves which renderer.info the perf overlay reads (pool is null here), which context textures/GLBs upload into, and — critically — that the exterior ALREADY runs a second WebGL context distinct from the pooled one used elsewhere. Any GLB texture-upload/perf-assert code wired to getPooledRenderer() will read a null or the wrong context. The whole draw-call/tri instrumentation gate is unbuildable until this is reconciled to the local renderer.
14. **mkPhys signature is fundamentally incompatible with post-load GLB material fixing — this recurs in ~8 workstreams and is never resolved at plan level** — Verified mobilePerf.ts:339-367: mkPhys(three, props) CONSTRUCTS a new material from a plain-props dict and RETURNS it; it cannot mutate/re-wrap a live GLTFLoader MeshStandardMaterial. Multiple WS (02,08,21,23,24,25) independently flag this as a blocker but each proposes its own ad-hoc fix (rebuild from PBR set, clone-then-strip, etc.). There is no single ratified post-load material contract. Without one shared helper (e.g. a real glbApplyMkPhys that reads existing maps off the loaded material and rebuilds), every workstream re-implements it differently, and the desktop path (mkPhys returns MeshPhysicalMaterial) will silently keep clearcoat/sheen the plan claims are stripped. This is a cross-cutting integration gap, not 28 independent bugs.
15. **loadModel().clone() shares geometry AND materials with the cached master → disposal and per-instance mutation corruption is systemic, not per-asset** — Verified modelLoader.ts:20/36 returns model.clone() (THREE shallow-clones materials+geometry by reference) and clearModelCache (50-64) disposes the master's geometry/materials. Any WS that (a) disposes a W3 group's geometry/materials at unmount, or (b) mutates clone.material.aoMap.channel / InstancedMesh geometry, corrupts the shared master and every future clone — including bust_base/bust_female which share the SAME cache. clearModelCache must NEVER be called at exterior unmount. The plan needs ONE ownership-manifest rule (clone materials before mutate; own only merged/instanced geometry) applied globally; today each WS reasons about it locally and several get it wrong.
16. **No draw-call/tri instrumentation exists AND the binding renderer.info is the local one — every 'net-negative draw calls' claim is unfalsifiable today** — ExteriorScene has zero renderer.info reads (grep confirmed). perfAssert.ts hardcodes MOBILE_DRAW_CALL_BUDGET=150 (not the plan's 80) and is gated on flag3d('w1_assert') and only branches on isMobileGPU — no desktop branch, no tri concept. Nearly every WS headline ('REPLACE → net calls ≤0') rests on the assumption that procedural dome/baluster/window primitives are separable and that hiding them frees draw calls. But ExteriorScene merges via mergeGeometries into ~18 static meshes; hiding a merged sub-geometry via visible=false frees NOTHING while adding a GLB is +1. The plan must land a STEP-0 instrumentation overlay AND a STEP-0 refactor extracting hero elements out of the merge BEFORE authoring — this ordering is asserted but not budgeted as a hard gate, and the 80-vs-150 budget discrepancy is unreconciled.
17. **DRACO decoder is COLD at exterior mount — busts load only in the interior bust-builder, so the first GLB triggers ~250KB wasm init inside the governor warmup window** — The 'decoder warm from bust GLBs' premise (repeated in WS01/03/04/09/25/27) is false for the exterior: bust GLBs load via the bust-builder panel, and ExteriorScene has zero loadModel calls today. First exterior GLB → cold DRACOLoader worker+wasm init mid-18s-dolly. dracoLoader is module-private in modelLoader.ts (no preload export). The plan needs a preloadDraco() export called as the very first W3 op AND must verify the worker initialises inside iOS WKWebView — neither is guaranteed to land before the reduced-motion still beats or the cinematic.
18. **Governor warmup/timing is misunderstood in multiple plans, and mid-dolly GLB decode+GPU-upload can trigger a persisted 7-day tier demotion** — Verified mobilePerf.ts: governor arms on first getQuality() (~mount), warmup is the first 2500ms WITHIN a 15000ms sample span (not additive; total ~15s from first rAF, not 17.5s or 15.5s from mount as different WS claim). A demotion PERSISTS to localStorage per-renderer-string for 7 days (readGovernorDemotion). GLTFLoader scene-graph build + GPU texture upload run on the MAIN thread in the resolve callback (only DRACO geometry decode is off-thread). A multi-atlas upload on an iPhone is a multi-frame hitch landing squarely in the sample window → >20% missed-frame windows → a real, sticky desktop→mobile or mobile→potato demotion the user carries for a week. No WS proposes a governor-audition-done handoff that is both correct (gate on sample completion, not a magic timer) and observable (mobilePerf exposes no getEffectiveTier/callback today).
19. **maxEagerTextureSets is NOT an enforced cap — it is read once as a boolean tier proxy; the 'mobile 4-set' safety net does not exist** — WS16 verified and WS16/WS15/WS07 depend on it: maxEagerTextureSets (mobile=4/potato=2/desktop=20) is consumed only as isMobileQ = Q.maxEagerTextureSets<=6 style tier detection at ExteriorScene:89. There is no counter, deferral queue, or 404-on-overflow. Mobile ALREADY synchronously loads clay_plaster+terracotta_tiles+painted_plaster+stone at mount (~279-297). Any new W3 PBR set is ADDITIVE GPU memory, not a 4-slot collapse. With toktx absent (KTX2 fast-follow inert), 4×4-channel×1k uncompressed JPG decode to ~48MB RGBA layered on ~60-80MB existing risks the ~140MB WKWebView ceiling. The plan's central texture-budget mitigation is machinery that must be BUILT (real eager accounting + deferral), not assumed.
20. **KTX2 is 'mandatory' in doctrine but unshippable in this environment — the mobile VRAM math has no compression backstop on ship day** — toktx is not on PATH (confirmed across WS04/16/17/19/20/24 audits); scripts/build-ktx2.mjs exists but produces nothing; no setKTX2Loader is wired into modelLoader (grep clean). GLB-embedded KTX2 without a registered transcoder is a SILENT decode failure — same class as the meshopt trap. The plan simultaneously says 'KTX2 atlases mandatory' for the 140MB ceiling AND sequences JPG/WEBP first. That is a contradiction: v1 must be PROVEN to hold 140MB with raw 1k JPG/WEBP (decodes to full RGBA in VRAM), or KTX2 must be installed and shipped in v1. Nobody has measured on-device GPU-resident bytes; the ceiling is paper-only.
21. **Reduced-motion path is a LIVE camera-jump crossfade in the render loop, not an offline still composer — GLBs must be resolved before ~t=resume or the name-beat still shows procedural fallback with no re-composite** — Verified ExteriorScene.tsx:4558-4584: W2 reduced-motion jumps the live camera through 3 stills (d=180/118/35) with a cream veil, inside the running rAF loop — there is no separate synchronous compositor that 'captures stills.' Several WS (15/17/18) say hero GLBs must be 'awaited before reduced-motion stills compose,' but the actual mechanism has no await hook: it fires on cinematic resume regardless of GLB load state. If a GLB resolves after the name-beat window (SHOT=2.4s, second still at d=118), the single most-read frame renders the procedural fallback and never redraws to the GLB (it's a timed cut, then handoff to entrance). The plan needs an explicit 'block/delay cinematic resume until hero GLBs loaded, or accept procedural at the name-beat' decision — currently unaddressed.
22. **flag3d() returns false during SSR and reads window.location.hostname — W3 gating semantics under Next.js hydration and the /concepts preview host are unspecified** — Verified flags3d.ts:41-47: flag3d returns false when window is undefined (SSR) and otherwise defaults ON for any non-prod hostname. The exterior is client-only so runtime is fine, but: (1) the plan never states W3 is read ONCE at mount into a const (per-frame flag reads would thrash sessionStorage parsing); (2) Vercel preview deploys and the /concepts board run on *.vercel.app hostnames, which are non-prod → W3 auto-ON there, so any half-finished W3 asset is live on every preview URL the owner opens to pick the exterior concept — a demo-integrity risk the plan doesn't flag. The prod seal depends solely on the two literal PROD_HOSTS strings; www vs apex is covered but any future custom domain silently enables W3.
23. **Two coexisting WebGL contexts on iOS (scene-local + pool) is a jetsam risk the plan inverts** — The doctrine says 'NEVER open a 2nd WebGL context (iOS jetsam kills it silently).' But the exterior ALREADY runs its own context (line 242-243) separate from the pooled renderer other scenes borrow. On SPA nav interior↔exterior, if the pooled context isn't disposed while the exterior's local one is live, iOS WKWebView can hold two GL contexts. Adding GLB streaming/upload on the local context increases its GPU footprint toward the jetsam threshold. The plan's 'use the pool, one context' guidance is not what the exterior does; the real integration must either migrate the exterior onto the pool (risky, touches the whole scene) or explicitly account for the two-context memory reality on iOS — neither is planned.
24. **Palette source-of-truth conflict: canon.ts GOLD=#D4AF37 vs the brief's bake target #B8973A, and coppo/travertine hexes absent from canon** — Verified via WS17/20/23 audits: canon.ts defines GOLD=#D4AF37 (emissive/frame token) while the brief instructs baking antique-gilt #B8973A; coppo #B0725A and travertine #E8DCC0 are brief values not present in canon. The shipped W2 dome is ochre #A5674E, not #B0725A. If parallel authoring agents bake to brief hexes, the GLBs will clash with adjacent procedural geometry AND with the #FFB870 sun grade. The plan needs a single ratified albedo ledger (baked-gold constant separate from emissive-gold, plus the ochre-vs-terracotta dome regrade decision) BEFORE any albedo bake — flagged as an open question but never closed, blocking every terracotta/gold asset.
25. **Cycles GPU (HIP) bake device is non-persistent and defaults to NONE/CPU — bakes silently fall to CPU and can time out over the MCP socket** — Multiple WS (04/12/25) note compute_device_type resets to NONE on every Blender/MCP restart, so AO/normal bakes silently run on CPU (slow, multi-minute) unless every authoring script re-asserts HIP+GPU. The bake+DRACO-export+header-assert pipeline has never been demonstrated end-to-end through the MCP socket; long bakes risk socket timeout/truncation. This is the unvalidated long pole of the entire program — the plan treats scripted geometry as low-risk (correct) but does not gate on a proven 1-tri bake→DRACO-export→KHR_draco_mesh_compression-header round-trip canary before committing to baked-AO-dependent mobile/potato shading (aoMap.channel=0 baked AO is the ONLY contact shadow on potato).
26. **aoMap UV-channel contract for GLB-loaded materials is unverified against GLTFLoader behavior** — assetLoader hardcodes aoMap.channel=0 for PROCEDURAL sets, but GLTFLoader-loaded textures carry glTF's own KHR_texture_transform / TEXCOORD channel mapping and modelLoader does NOT normalise it (verified modelLoader only sets castShadow/receiveShadow). If a baked AO is exported on UV0 but GLTFLoader maps aoMap to UV1 (default glTF occlusion convention), mobile/potato — which depend entirely on baked AO for contact shadow — will sample the wrong/absent UV and read flat. The plan asserts 'bake AO on UV0, channel=0 hardcoded' but never verifies that the runtime GLB material actually reads channel 0 after load; this needs an explicit post-load aoMap.channel=0 pass (guarded to run once on the shared cached material to avoid the clone double-apply race).
27. **No living light / no time-of-day motion — the scene is a frozen postcard, and 'golden hour' is asserted but never earns the wow** — The entire 1000x thesis rests on golden-hour mood, yet the plan is 28 workstreams of STATIC masonry geometry plus a code-only post-grade. The moodboard's actual emotional payload (m2/m3 San Quirico 'al tramonto', the west-flank-on-fire / east-flank-in-ink RATIO the analysis calls 'het compositie-instrument') is a LIGHTING phenomenon, and daylightCycle.ts already exists but no workstream animates the sun across the 18s dolly, adds god-rays/volumetric shafts through the cypress avenue, drifting shadow, warm atmospheric haze deepening with distance, or bloom blooming as the lantern catches the sun at the name-beat. A owner who asked for 'golden hour' and 'you'd be surprised to find this' will see crisper stone and say 'nice model' — not 'wow, it's ALIVE.' The single highest wow-per-effort lever (moving/volumetric light + atmosphere) is absent from all 28 workstreams; WS18 is only a static HDRI swap + AO bake.
28. **Zero micro-motion / no signs of life — nothing moves, so it reads as an architectural render, not a place** — The moodboard sells cypresses at sunset, a lived-in borgo 'gegroeid nei secoli.' Nothing in the plan moves except the camera. There is no wind in the cypress/wheat/grass (WS14 ships static billboards; existing grassShader wind isn't wired to a hero moment), no water motion in the hero fountain (WS12 explicitly keeps water procedural and defers cascade/RTT — the fountain is the #5 hero yet the water just sits), no drifting birds/swifts over the dome, no smoke from the chimney pots WS10 ships, no flag/banner, no distant flicker. Stillness is the #1 tell of 'CGI model' vs 'real place.' A 1000x perceived lift almost always comes from ambient life, and the plan has none.
29. **The name-beat (WP3, 7.5s) — the single most-read frame and the owner's personal payoff — has no authored 'wow' treatment** — Every brief calls WP3 the most-read frame and the emotional climax (the owner's own name on the gold tympanum, framed between the two gate-towers). The plan treats it as a geometry problem: acanthus capitals, drum windows, a gold-frame GLB, extruded lettering. But nothing choreographs a MOMENT there — no lens/DOF rack-focus onto the name, no gold specular glint/anamorphic catch as the sun rays align, no subtle bloom pulse, no atmospheric separation pushing the towers back so the name floats. WS26 (dolly choreography) even flags its own '18 draw calls' premise as false and hasn't measured the baseline. If the owner's name doesn't land as a spine-tingling beat, the owner will feel the whole thing is competent but cold — the exact failure mode of 'still not 1000x.'
30. **Cohesion risk: bright, crisp GLB heroes dropped onto untouched low-fi procedural surroundings will look like collage, not one world** — The plan surgically replaces ~7 hero elements (dome, drum windows, capitals, balustrades, fountain) but leaves terrain, grass, cypresses (mobile), distant landscape, sky, and most wall surfaces procedural and unchanged. Palette canon is contested across briefs (GOLD #D4AF37 in canon.ts vs #B8973A in the spec; dome ochre #A5674E shipped vs #B0725A authored — WS02 flags this as an unresolved owner decision that 'blocks final albedo bake'). If the new baked-AO stone reads sharper and warmer than the adjacent procedural coppo roofs and flat terrain, the eye locks onto the SEAM, and perceived quality can go DOWN in the transition zones. A 1000x jump requires the WHOLE frame to lift together (or a deliberate depth-of-field/atmosphere veil to hide the low-fi background), and no workstream owns scene-wide cohesion or the regrade.
31. **'Grown over centuries' (P3/P4, the owner's explicit ask) is a massing-plan promise the asset plan never delivers in surface texture** — The moodboard's core thesis and three of the four owner pain-points (P2 towers-as-fence, P3 too little borgo-feel, P4 surprise/volume) are about ORGANIC, weathered, age-varied character. The plan delivers clean parametric geometry with shared trim-sheet atlases and 'jitter for asymmetry.' But 'gegroeid nei secoli' lives in surface storytelling: differential weathering (water-staining below sills, moss in north shadows, spalled plaster showing brick, lichen on north tower faces, uneven settling, patched-over openings, varied roof-tile discoloration). WS05 even flags that its worn-limewash swap repaints the WHOLE corps uniformly — defeating the varied-patina goal — as the load-bearing unresolved blocker. Uniform cleanliness reads as 'new build / videogame,' the opposite of the approved aesthetic; the owner asked specifically NOT to look diagrammatic.
32. **Foreground richness / human scale is missing — nothing near the camera to anchor the 1000x read at the arrival beats** — Perceived quality is dominated by what fills the near-frame at WP1/WP4/WP5 (the arrival approach up the cypress avenue and stair). The plan's foreground is: procedural gravel, buxus balls, a parterre urn, and a stair. There are no hero foreground props at human scale (weathered terracotta planters with real plants, a stone bench with worn edges, ivy actually climbing a wall with parallax depth, fallen leaves/petals, a well-head, garden tools, a lantern on the door) — the incidental detail that signals craftsmanship up close. WS13 gardens are P2/desktop-only and WS11 cortile is P3/occluded. Distant crisp architecture with an empty, sparse foreground is the classic 'good model, dead scene' — the owner will feel the emptiness even if they can't name it.
33. **No reference-locked target or side-by-side acceptance bar — '1000x' is unfalsifiable and per-asset fidelity is unmeasured** — The goal is explicitly ~1000x perceived quality, but there is no authored hero reference frame (a rendered still of the desired end-state at WP3), no before/after comparison gate, and no aesthetic sign-off checkpoint — only technical budgets (tris/draw-calls/fps). Multiple workstreams (WS19, WS26) admit the draw-call baseline was never even measured. Worse, the two assets most responsible for the emotional 'wow' (fountain mascaron and any statuary/figural life) depend on Hunyuan3D/Rodin which are DISABLED across every workstream, so v1 ships scripted lathe-of-revolution placeholders — WS19 itself concedes the scripted tazza is 'NOT a ~1000x lift for that specific asset.' Without a locked visual target and a figural/statuary path, the owner has no frame to say 'yes, this is it,' and the most likely verdict is 'sharper, but still not what I pictured.'
